one should roast it seven times in an earthen shard placed on a stove,

children.text: agnivarṇaṃ bhavedyāvad vāraṃ vāraṃ ca cūrṇayet ||
children.translated_text: until it becomes fire-colored, powdering it each time again and again.
One should continue roasting until a blade of grass thrown in is burned.
Then, after grinding it with sulphur in a decoction of banyan root,
one should cook it twenty times with a boar <s>puṭa</s> furnace-charge,
and again twenty times with a decoction produced from <s>Triphala</s>.
Having impregnated it with <s>Triphala</s>, <s>Muṇḍikā</s>, <s>Bhṛṅga</s>, <s>Pathyā</s>, <s>Nīlī</s>, and <s>Sumūlaka</s>,
it should be administered in measured doses for all diseases.
It is only slightly inferior to mica <s>sattva</s>, unaltered and very rich in qualities.
If it is prepared in this way a hundred times by <s>puṭa</s>-cooking,
it becomes exceedingly efficacious, the supreme agent for digestion and kindling appetite.
When taken in a dose of half a <s>guñjā</s>, it produces hunger in a very strong degree;
combined with formulations that remove each particular disease, it cuts down all diseases.
<s>Dhānyābhra</s> triturated with the juice of <s>Kāsamarda</s>
should be cooked a hundred times; it is thereby killed, without doubt.
Likewise with the juice of <s>Mustā</s> and also with the juice of <s>Taṇḍulīya</s>;
mica made into discs, ground with <s>Śivā</s>, <s>Āmalaka</s>, and <s>Saubhāgya</s>,
should be cooked sixty times; it becomes like vermilion.
According to the formulation and vehicle, it becomes a destroyer of wasting disease and other internal ailments.
In a decoction of banyan-root bark, in the extract of betel leaves,
or with <s>Vāsā</s> and <s>Matsyākṣikī</s>, or with <s>Matsyākṣī</s> together with <s>Kaṭhillā</s>,
the <s>ghana</s> triturated with the milk-sap of the banyan tree and cooked
becomes, after twenty rounds, a <s>ghana</s> resembling vermilion.

children.text: saṭaṅkaṇaṃ gavāṃ dugdhaiḥ piṣṭaṃ prapuṭitaṃ ghanam
children.translated_text: The <s>ghana</s>, ground with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> in cow's milk and thoroughly cooked,
becomes free from glitter after thirty rounds and is better endowed with qualities.

children.text: evaṃ siddhāni cābhrāṇi tālena puṭitāni cet
children.translated_text: If the micas perfected in this way are cooked with <s>tāla</s> (orpiment),
they become extremely sharp in action, and stronger even than <s>rasa</s>.
Dryness, subtlety, floating on water, and the arising of a red color,
as well as the brilliance of varied qualities, arise through many <s>puṭa</s>-cookings.
With the separate juices of <s>Kāsamarda</s>, <s>Ghanadhvani</s>, <s>Vāsā</s>, and <s>Punarbhu</s>,
and of <s>Matsyākṣī</s>, <s>Kāravellī</s>, and <s>Haṃsapādī</s>,
one should grind it carefully again and again and dry it by the heat of the sun.
Oilcake, wheat flour, small fish, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
each in a quantity equal to the mica, should be added and triturated well.
At every trituration one should dry it thoroughly with the rays of the sun.
The five products of goats, the five products of cows, and the five products of buffaloes
should be added, and balls should be made, somewhat the size of <s>tinduka</s> fruits.

children.text: payo dadhi ghṛtaṃ mūtraṃ viṭ ca pañcāṅgam ucyate
children.translated_text: Milk, curd, ghee, urine, and dung are called the fivefold product.
In a downward-falling furnace one should smelt it and cause the <s>sattva</s> to descend.

children.text: koṣṭhyāḥ kiṭṭaṃ samāhṛtya vicūrṇya ravakān haret
children.translated_text: Having collected the slag from the furnace, one should pulverize it and remove the small grains.
That slag should be triturated with a little <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> and cow dung.
Having made balls and dried them, one should smelt them again as before.
Again collecting the slag, one should triturate it and recover the <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: evameva punaḥ kiṭṭaṃ dhmātvā sattvaṃ samāharet
children.translated_text: In just this way one should again smelt the slag and collect the <s>sattva</s>.
Then those grains of <s>sattva</s>, after being boiled with sour gruel,
should be sealed inside a crucible together with the purifying group of substances.

children.text: samyag drutaṃ samāhṛtya dvivāraṃ pradhamet punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having gathered it when it is properly melted, one should blow it again twice.
Thus the <s>sattva</s> becomes perfected and is fit for use in <s>rasa</s> and <s>rasāyana</s>.
When it has been melted in honey, oil, fat, and ghee and repeatedly quenched,
the hard <s>sattva</s> of iron and other metals becomes soft after ten rounds.
The ball of <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence), when heated, should be put into sour gruel combined with <s>sasyaka</s>.
After quenching it, at that very moment one should break it up with an iron implement.
Having thoroughly heated the thick, coarse particles and thrown them into sour gruel,
one should gather them immediately, crush them, and make them into powder.
Then that powder should be fried with cow's ghee three times, as before.
Likewise, this should be done with the juice of <s>dhātrī</s> fruit, or with the juice of <s>dhātrī</s> leaves.
At each frying, grinding on a stone slab should be performed.
After that, with juices of <s>Punarnavā</s> and <s>Vāsā</s> mixed with sour gruel,
one should give it <s>puṭa</s> (sealed heating) ten times, and ten times with sulfur.
Thus prepared, <s>vyomasattva</s> (mica essence) is supreme in all qualities.
It may be used as desired in <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation) and in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation).

children.text: vellavyoṣasamanvitaṃ ghṛtayutaṃ vallonmitaṃ sevitaṃ divyābhraṃ kṣayapāṇḍuruggrahaṇikāḥ śūlāmakoṣṭhāmayam
children.translated_text: Divine mica, combined with <s>vella</s> and <s>vyoṣa</s>, mixed with ghee, and taken in a <s>valla</s> measure, overcomes wasting disease, pallor, disorders of <s>grahaṇī</s>, colic, and abdominal disease from undigested matter.

children.text: jūrtiṃ śvāsagadaṃ pramehamaruciṃ kāsāmayaṃ durdharaṃ mandāgniṃ jaṭharavyathāṃ vijayate yogairaśeṣāmayān ||
children.translated_text: It conquers feverish debility, asthma, urinary disease, loss of appetite, obstinate cough, weak digestion, abdominal pain, and, through proper formulas, every disease.

children.text: drutayo naiva nirdiṣṭāḥ śāstre dṛṣṭā api dhruvam
children.translated_text: Liquefactions are not taught in the treatise, even though they are certainly observed.

children.text: vinā śambhoḥ prasādena na sidhyanti kathañcana ||
children.translated_text: Without the grace of <s>Śambhu</s>, they can in no way succeed.
<s>Rājāvarta</s> has little redness and a luster mixed with reddish blue.
The best is heavy and smooth; another kind is considered middling.
<s>Rājāvarta</s> removes urinary disease, wasting, <s>durnāma</s>, pallor, phlegm, and wind.
It kindles appetite, digests, is aphrodisiac, and is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
Minerals such as <s>rājāvarta</s>, when steamed with lemon juices, cow urine, and alkalis,
are indeed purified by two or three repetitions.
Powdered <s>rājāvarta</s>, supplied with <s>bhṛṅga</s> water and sulfur,
becomes killed, that is, calcined, by <s>puṭa</s> heating for seven nights.
<s>Sūryāvarttaka</s>, <s>Vajrakanda</s>, <s>Kadalī</s>, <s>Koṣātakī</s>, and <s>Śigrukā</s>,

children.text: vandhyā nīrakaṇā ghanā nṛpaśamī dhvāṃkṣī kumārī varā
children.translated_text: <s>Vandhyā</s>, <s>Nīrakaṇā</s>, <s>Ghanā</s>, <s>Nṛpaśamī</s>, <s>Dhvāṃkṣī</s>, excellent <s>Kumārī</s>,
by the single juice of these, together with sour <s>puṭa</s> heating, metals and the like are purified.
They undergo sweating, moistening, and killing; then, when blown in the furnace again, those substances yield their essences.
This method purifies without remainder the impurities of all metals.
With alkalis and salts, house-soot, <s>guñjā</s>, and fruits of <s>Niśā</s>,
stones and mineral ores, when joined with these, release their essence completely.
Eight-cornered, eight-faced, six-angled, smooth, and heavy,
and endowed with pure and mixed colors: this is called <s>vaikrānta</s>.
It is white, red, yellow, blue, pigeon-colored,
dark, black, and variegated; thus it is eightfold.
<s>Vaikrāntaka</s> gives life, produces strength and complexion, is highly aphrodisiac, grants intelligence, and removes all disorders of the humors.

children.text: dīptāgnikṛt pavisamānaguṇas tarasvī vaikrāntakaḥ khalu vapurbalalohakārī ||
children.translated_text: It kindles the digestive fire, has qualities equal to the thunderbolt, is powerful, and produces bodily strength and firmness like iron.
Among all <s>rasāyana</s> substances, <s>vaikrānta</s> is foremost and mighty.
It should be used in place of diamond; it removes every disease.
<s>Vaikrānta</s>, thoroughly steamed in a decoction of horse gram, is purified.
It is killed in eight <s>puṭa</s> heatings when combined with sulfur and lemon juice.
By the method for extracting essence, it is triturated and made into pellets.
Placed in a crucible and blown for one <s>ghaṭikā</s>, <s>vaikrānta</s> releases its essence.

children.text: bhasmatvaṃ samupāgato vikṛtako hemnā mṛtenānvitaḥ pādāṃśena kaṇājyavellasahito vallonmitaḥ sevitaḥ
children.translated_text: When reduced to ash and transformed, combined with calcined gold in a quarter portion, together with pepper, ghee, and <s>vella</s>, and taken in a <s>valla</s> measure,

children.text: yakṣmāṇaṃ kṣaraṇaṃ ca pāṇḍugudajaṃ śvāsaṃ ca kāsāmayaṃ duṣṭāṃ ca grahaṇīm uraḥkṣatamukhān rogāñjayeddehakṛt ||
children.translated_text: it conquers consumption, wasting, pallor, rectal disease, asthma, cough, bad <s>grahaṇī</s>, chest wounds, and related diseases, and it builds up the body.
Blue <s>vaikrānta</s> ash, combined with half as much ash of <s>sūta</s> (mercury),
and calcined mica-essence equal to both, should be thoroughly triturated.
Mixed with honey and ghee and taken in the morning in a <s>guñjā</s> measure,
according to the <s>rasāyana</s> regimen, one would live as long as the moon, sun, and stars.
Taken in a barley-grain measure with a vehicle appropriate to each disease,
it destroys all diseases that are difficult to cross with other medicines.
For human beings, within three times seven days, it acts like the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> upon sin.
Having drunk <s>Hālāhala</s> poison, <s>Garutmat</s>, who had drunk nectar, vomited it out.
That poison, joined with nectar, on the mountain called <s>Marut</s>,

children.text: tadvāntaṃ hi ghanībhūtaṃ saṃjātaṃ sasyakaṃ khalu ||
children.translated_text: became solidified from that vomit and indeed turned into <s>sasyaka</s>.
That which has the true hue of a peacock's neck and is very heavy is especially praised.
Just as poison joined with another substance takes on the stronger qualities of that substance,
so <s>Hālāhala</s> joined with nectar has the superior qualities of nectar.
Here <s>mayūratuttha</s> is said to remove all doṣas and poison, to relieve rectal pain, colic, corrupted acid-pitta, and constipation, and to be beneficial.

children.text: rāsāyanaṃ vamanarekakaraṃ garaghnaṃ śvitrāpahaṃ gaditamatra mayūratuttham ||
children.translated_text: It is a <s>rasāyana</s>, causes vomiting and purging, destroys artificial poison, and removes white leprosy.
<s>Sasyaka</s>, well steamed in a swing apparatus for three watches,
is purified with the urines of humans, buffaloes, goats, and cows; thus <s>sasyaka</s> is purified.
Combined with <s>lakuca</s> juice, sulfur, stone, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
and sealed inside a crucible, it is killed by chicken-dung <s>puṭa</s> heatings.
Sealed inside a crucible with lemon juice and a little <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
and heated all around, <s>sasyaka</s> releases a copper-like essence.
Purified <s>sasyaka</s>, passed through fire and combined with the previous medicines,
certainly releases its essence by the method of blowing through a tube.
Having taken this essence and joined it with excellent <s>bhūnāga</s> essence,
a ring made from it, when brought into contact, immediately becomes a remover of pain.

children.text: carācaraṃ viṣaṃ bhūtaṃ ḍākinīṃ dṛggataṃ jayet
children.translated_text: It conquers moving and unmoving poison, beings, ḍākinīs, and afflictions that have entered the eye.
The syllables are likewise: '<s>rāmavat somasenānī mudrikā</s>'.
This <s>mudrā</s> should be made; it produces visible proof of its effect.
On the northern side of the <s>Himālaya</s> there is a great tree named <s>Aśvakarṇa</s>.

children.text: tatra śūlaṃ samutpannaṃ tatraiva nidhanaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: There a piercing pain arose, and there itself it came to its end.
Water marked with the <s>mudrā</s>, drunk after being enchanted seven times with this mantra,
is said to remove piercing pain at once; so <s>Bhāluki</s> spoke.
Oil heated by means of this <s>mudrā</s>, certainly over fire,

children.text: lepitaṃ hanti vegena śūlaṃ yatra kvacidbhavam
children.translated_text: when smeared on, quickly destroys piercing pain wherever it has arisen.
It immediately brings on delivery for a woman and at once removes pain of the eyes.
<s>Vimala</s> is said to be threefold: beginning with the golden kind, then the silver kind.
The third is bronze <s>vimala</s>; it is recognized by the lustre proper to each.
Round, furnished with angles, smooth, and provided with flat plates:
<s>vimala</s> removes wind and bile, is aphrodisiac, and is an excellent <s>rasāyana</s>.
The first is said to be suited to operations on gold, the second is considered effective for making silver,
and the third is for medicines; among these, each earlier one is superior in qualities to the following.
Steamed in the juice of <s>Āṭarūṣa</s>, <s>vimala</s> becomes pure <s>vimala</s>.
With <s>gandhāśman</s> and <s>lakuca</s>, it is killed by ten <s>puṭa</s>s.
With the liquids of <s>saṭaṅka</s> and <s>lakuca</s>, and with ash of ram's horn,

children.text: piṣṭo mūṣodare liptaḥ saṃśoṣya ca nirudhya ca ||
children.translated_text: it is ground, smeared inside a crucible, dried, and then sealed up.
Blown with six <s>prastha</s>s of charcoal, <s>vimala</s> releases an essence resembling lead.

children.text: sattvaṃ muñcati tadyukto rasaḥ syāttu rasāyanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> joined with that becomes a <s>rasāyana</s>.
Having combined this essence with <s>sūta</s> and made it into a paste, it should be well triturated.
After casting it into melted sulfur, one should digest three times its quantity of mica.
And also five times the quantity of <s>śilā</s> in a tubular apparatus, indeed;
silver ash in a tenth part, and just as much dead <s>vaikrāntaka</s>.
Having powdered all this together and strained it through cloth,
one should put it into a glass bottle and fill it carefully.

children.text: līḍho vyoṣavarānvito vimalako yukto ghṛtaiḥ sevito hanyād durbhagakṛjjvarān śvayathukaṃ pāṇḍupramehārucim
children.translated_text: When <s>vimalaka</s>, licked with <s>vyoṣa</s> and <s>varā</s>, joined with ghee and taken, it destroys fevers that cause misery, swelling, anemia, urinary disease, and loss of appetite.

children.text: mūlārtiṃ grahaṇīṃ ca śūlamatulaṃ yakṣmāmayān kāmalāṃ sarvānpittamarudgadān kimaparaṃ yogairaśeṣān gadān ||
children.translated_text: It also destroys rectal pain, bowel disorder, unsurpassed colic, wasting diseases, jaundice, all disorders of bile and wind, and, what more, through its applications all diseases without remainder.
<s>Śilādhātu</s> is said to be of two kinds: the first, beginning with cow's urine, is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
The other begins with camphor; of these, the first is again twofold.
One has essence and the other is without essence; of the two, the former is superior in qualities.
In summer, from the slopes of the snow-bearing mountain, heated by the fierce sun,
<s>śilādhātu</s> flows forth from mountains containing gold, silver, and copper.
That born from a gold-bearing mountain is heavy and resembles a hibiscus flower.
It is slightly bitter, very sweet, and that is the supreme <s>rasāyana</s>.
That born from a silver-bearing mountain is sweet, pale, and heavy.
<s>Śilāja</s> destroys bilious disease and especially removes anemia.
That born from a copper-bearing mountain is blue in color, dense, and heavy.
<s>Śilāja</s>, bitter and hot, destroys phlegm and wind and removes wasting disease.
When thrown into fire, that which assumes the shape of a liṅga and is smokeless,

children.text: salile'tha vilīnaṃ ca tacchuddhaṃ hi śilājatu ||
children.translated_text: and then dissolves in water: that indeed is pure <s>śilājatu</s>.

children.text: nūnaṃ sajvarapāṇḍuśophaśamanaṃ mehāgnimāndyāpahaṃ medaśchedakaraṃ ca yakṣmaśamanaṃ mūtrāmayonmūlanam
children.translated_text: It certainly allays fever, anemia, and swelling; removes urinary disease and weak digestion; cuts away fat; quiets consumption; and uproots disorders of urine.

children.text: gulmaplīhavināśanaṃ jaṭharahṛcchūlaghnam āmāpahaṃ sarvatvaggadanāśanaṃ kimaparaṃ dehe ca lohe hitam ||
children.translated_text: It destroys abdominal tumors and spleen disease, removes abdominal colic, destroys colic, removes undigested humors, and destroys all skin diseases; what more, it is beneficial for the body and for metal.
Whatever qualities exist in <s>rasa</s>, secondary minerals, <s>sūta</s>, jewels, and metals,
they dwell in <s>śilādhātu</s>, because of the desire to conquer old age and death.
Placed in a steaming apparatus with alkalis, acids, and <s>guggulu</s>,
and steamed for the measure of a <s>ghaṭikā</s>, <s>śilādhātu</s> is purified.
With <s>śilā</s>, sulfur, and orpiment, and with citron juice,
<s>śilādhātu</s>, subjected to heating, is killed by eight <s>giriṇḍaka</s>s.

children.text: bhasmībhūtaśilodbhavaṃ samatulaṃ kāntaṃ ca vaikrāntakaṃ yuktaśca triphalākaṭutrayaghṛtairvallena tulyaṃ bhajet
children.translated_text: One should take ash-born <s>śilā</s> in equal measure, together with <s>kānta</s> and <s>vaikrāntaka</s>, combined with <s>triphala</s>, the three pungents, and ghee, in an equal <s>valla</s> dose.

children.text: pāṇḍau yakṣmagude tathāgnisadane maheṣu mūtrāmaye gulmaplīhamahodare bahuvidhe śūle ca yonyāmaye ||
children.translated_text: It is to be used for anemia, consumption, rectal disease, loss of digestive fire, urinary disorders, abdominal tumors, spleen disease, great abdominal enlargement, many kinds of colic, and diseases of the womb.
If one takes it for six months according to the <s>rasāyana</s> procedure,
freed from wrinkles and grey hair, one lives happily for a hundred years.
The mountain-born substance, ground with the acidic group of liquefying agents,

children.text: liptvā mūṣodare ruddhvā gāḍhairdhmātaṃ hi kokilaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be smeared inside a crucible, sealed, and strongly blown with charcoal.
<s>Śilādhātu</s> releases an essence from its own mine, resembling metal.
The camphor-first <s>śilājatu</s> is pale and sand-like.
It destroys strangury, urinary stones, urinary disease, jaundice, and anemia.
Steamed with cardamom water and dried, it attains purification.
The wise have prescribed no killing or extraction of essence for this.
<s>Rasaka</s> is said to be twofold: <s>dardura</s> and <s>kāravellaka</s>.
The <s>dardura</s> is said to have layers; the <s>kāravellaka</s> has no layers.
The first is excellent for extracting essence, and the second for medicines and the like.
<s>Rasaka</s> destroys all urinary diseases and eliminates phlegm and bile.
It also destroys eye disease and wasting disease, and colors iron and mercury.
<s>Nāgārjuna</s> has taught both <s>rasa</s> and <s>rasaka</s>.
The two are the best perfected rasas, supreme agents for the body and for metal.
By whomever both <s>rasa</s> (mercury) and <s>rasaka</s> are made able to withstand fire,
accomplishment with respect to the body and metals is his servant; there is no doubt.
A <s>kharpara</s>, thoroughly heated and immersed seven times
in the juice of <s>bījapūra</s> (citron), obtains purity.

children.text: nṛmūtre meṣamūtre vā takre vā kāñjike tathā
children.translated_text: In human urine, or in sheep's urine, or in buttermilk, and likewise in sour gruel,
when heated strongly and properly immersed, <s>kharpara</s> becomes purified.

children.text: naramūtre sthito māsaṃ rasako rañjayed dhruvam
children.translated_text: <s>Rasaka</s> kept for a month in human urine will certainly color

children.text: śuddhaṃ tāmraṃ rasaṃ tāraṃ śuddhaṃ svarṇaprabhaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: purified copper, <s>rasa</s> (mercury), silver, and purified metal with a golden lustre.
With <s>haridrā</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>ārāla</s>, <s>sindhu</s>, fumes, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
together with <s>āruṣkara</s>, each in quarter parts, and with acidic substances, one should triturate the <s>kharpara</s>.
After it has been smeared on an eggplant-shaped crucible, dried, and sealed,
one should place the <s>kharpara</s> over the mouth of the crucible and then blow strongly.
When the <s>kharpara</s> has been removed, if the flame becomes blue or white,

children.text: tadā sandaṃśato mūṣāṃ dhṛtvā kṛtvā hyadhomukhīm ||
children.translated_text: then, holding the crucible with tongs and turning it face downward,

children.text: śanairāsphālayed bhūmau yathā nālaṃ na bhajyate
children.translated_text: one should gently strike it on the ground so that the tube is not broken.
The <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence), fallen out like tin, should then be taken and applied.

children.text: evaṃ hi tricaturvāraiḥ sarvaṃ sattvaṃ viniḥsaret
children.translated_text: In this way, through three or four repetitions, all the <s>sattva</s> comes out.
Or else one should bury a pot filled with water in the belly of the furnace.
On its mouth one should set a perforated vessel, and on that mouth place an inverted crucible.
Then one should put burning coals over the crucible and blow strongly.
Taking the <s>sattva</s> that has fallen into the water of the pot, one should employ it.
Putting that <s>sattva</s>, combined with <s>tālaka</s>, into a <s>kharpara</s>,
one should roast it with an iron rod; it certainly becomes ash.
That ash, combined with an equal amount of incinerated <s>kānta</s> iron,
as powder measuring eight <s>guñjā</s>, mixed with a decoction of <s>triphalā</s>,
kept at night in an iron vessel and given with sesame preparation,
when taken, quickly destroys even <s>madhumeha</s> (diabetes), certainly,

children.text: paittaṃ kṣayaṃ ca pāṇḍuṃ ca śvayathuṃ gulmameva ca ||
children.translated_text: as well as bilious wasting, anemia, swelling, and <s>gulma</s>.
It also destroys bloody <s>gulma</s> in women, excessive uterine discharge, and <s>somaroga</s>,
all disorders of the womb, and intermittent fevers as well,

children.text: rajaḥśūlaṃ ca nārīṇāṃ kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ ca hidhmikām ||
children.translated_text: menstrual pain in women, cough, dyspnea, and hiccup.
<s>Mākṣika</s> is of two kinds: gold <s>mākṣika</s> and silver <s>mākṣika</s>.
Of these, the first <s>mākṣika</s> comes from <s>Kānyakubja</s> and resembles gold.
That produced on the bank of the <s>Tapatī</s> is like five-colored gold.
The one full of stone is said to be called <s>tāpya</s>; it has little virtue.

children.text: mākṣīkadhātuḥ sakalāmayaghnaḥ prāṇo rasendrasya paraṃ hi vṛṣyaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> ore destroys every disease; it is truly the life of <s>rasendra</s> (mercury) and is supremely aphrodisiac.
It also joins two metals that are hard to combine; excellent in qualities, it is foremost among all rasāyanas.
<s>Mākṣika</s> is purified when cooked in castor oil and citron water.
When it is cooked for two <s>ghaṭikā</s> in water from a banana bulb,
then heated and thrown into a decoction of <s>varā</s>, <s>mākṣika</s> attains purification.
Ground with citron juice and sulfur and placed inside a crucible,
<s>mākṣika</s>, burnt with five <s>kroḍa</s>-heatings, is indeed killed.
With castor oil, cow ghee, and citron juice,
when firmly cooked in a <s>kharpara</s>, it becomes like metal.
Thus killed, it is to be used with <s>rasa</s> and also in the rasāyana procedure.
Combined with a thirtieth part of <s>nāga</s> and treated with alkalis and acids,
<s>mākṣika</s>, blown in an open crucible, releases its <s>sattva</s>.
<s>Nāga</s>, repeatedly melted seven times and thrown into the juice of <s>nirguṇḍikā</s>,
when mixed with <s>mākṣika-sattva</s>, certainly loses its nature.
The purified <s>tāpya-sattva</s>, having a color like <s>guñjā</s> seed and melting quickly like lead,
is supreme for effecting the body and metals.

children.text: mākṣīkasattvena rasasya piṣṭīṃ kṛtvā vilīne ca baliṃ nidhāya
children.translated_text: Having made a paste of <s>rasa</s> with <s>mākṣika-sattva</s>, and, when it is molten, having placed the offering,

children.text: saṃmiśrya saṃmardya ca khalvamadhye nikṣipya sattvaṃ drutamabhrakasya ca ||
children.translated_text: one should mix and triturate it in a mortar, and add the quickly molten <s>sattva</s> of <s>abhraka</s>.

children.text: vidhāya golaṃ lavaṇākhyayantre paceddinārdhaṃ mṛduvahninā ca
children.translated_text: Making it into a ball, one should cook it in the apparatus called <s>lavaṇa</s> for half a day with a gentle fire.

children.text: svataḥ suśītaṃ paricūrṇya samyag vallonmitaṃ khaṇḍaviḍaṅgayuktam ||
children.translated_text: When it has cooled by itself, one should powder it well; a <s>valla</s> measure, joined with sugar and <s>viḍaṅga</s>,

children.text: saṃsevitaṃ kṣaudrayutaṃ nihanti jarāṃ sarogām apamṛtyumeva
children.translated_text: taken with honey, destroys diseased old age and even premature death.
It destroys even hard-to-cure diseases in seven doses; not even nectar-essence is equal to this.
Incinerated <s>mākṣika</s> stone is the base; half of that is incinerated <s>abhraka</s>,
half of that is <s>kānta</s> iron, and half of that is copper ash.
Combining everything together, one should add an equal amount of sulfur.
After triturating with lemon juice, one should heat it in a closed <s>puṭa</s> ten times.
Pulverizing it, one should process it with exactly one hundred forest cow-dung cakes.
Then one should levigate it twenty-one times with the water of <s>vyoṣa</s> and <s>bāhlīka</s>.
This becomes incinerated <s>mākṣika</s>, destroyer of all diseases.

children.text: kṣayaṃ pāṇḍuṃ ca kuṣṭhāni grahaṇīṃ gudajāṃ rujaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It destroys wasting, anemia, skin diseases, <s>grahaṇī</s>, and disorders of the anus,
weak digestion, jaundice, emaciation, loss of voice, and anorexia,
fierce fevers of many forms, <s>āmadoṣa</s>, and cholera,
and all the various diseases arising from wind, bile, and phlegm without remainder,
when used with suitable accompanying drinks according to each particular case.
Among all the <s>mahārasa</s> substances, <s>tāpya</s> alone is considered the best.
The substances named <s>gandhāśma</s>, <s>tāla</s>, <s>tuvarī</s>, <s>kunaṭī</s>, <s>sauvīra</s>, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, <s>khecara</s>, and <s>gairika</s>

children.text: uktā budhairuparasāśca rasāyanāste tairbaddhapāradavaro na rasāyanaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: are called by the wise <s>uparasa</s> substances and rasāyanas; without them, even excellent bound mercury would not be a rasāyana.

children.text: caturdhā gandhako jñeyo varṇaiḥ śvetādibhiḥ khalu
children.translated_text: Sulfur should be known as fourfold, according to colors beginning with white.
Here the white is called chalky; it is used for smearing and for the killing of metals.
Likewise there is the variety called <s>Amalasāra</s>, which is yellow in color.
That same one is <s>Śukapiccha</s>; it is the best in mercury-<s>rasāyana</s>.
The red, called <s>Śukatuṇḍa</s>, is excellent in the procedure of transmuting metals.
The black-colored one is rare, and it destroys old age and death.

children.text: gandhāśmātirasāyanaḥ samadhuraḥ pāke kaṭūṣṇānvitaḥ kaṇḍūkuṣṭhavisarpadadrudamano dīptānalaḥ pācanaḥ
children.translated_text: Sulfur-stone is an excellent <s>rasāyana</s>, evenly sweet, and in digestion pungent and hot; it suppresses itching, skin disease, erysipelas, and ringworm, kindles the digestive fire, and promotes digestion.

children.text: āmonmocanaśoṣaṇo viṣaharaḥ sūtendravīryaprado gaurīpuṣpabhavastathā krimiharaḥ sattvātmakaḥ sūtajit ||
children.translated_text: It releases, dries up, and removes undigested matter, counteracts poison, gives potency to lordly mercury, is born from <s>Gaurīpuṣpa</s>, destroys worms, is essence-natured, and conquers mercury.
In former times it was used by mighty <s>Bali</s> as a source of abundant strength.
As he was dragging <s>Vāsuki</s>, his fat was melted by the flame from that serpent's mouth.
That fat, rich in the odor of sulfur, flowed out everywhere from his body.
It attained the state of sulfur; therefore the sulfurous smell became poisonous.
For that reason sulfur is called the fat of <s>Bali</s>, and it is very pleasing.
Sulfur, steamed in milk for one <s>ghaṭī</s> and washed with water,
then melted with cow's ghee and filtered through cloth, attains purification.
When purified in this way, it should cast off its stones in the cloth.

children.text: ghṛte viṣaṃ tuṣākāraṃ svayaṃ piṇḍatvameti ca
children.translated_text: In the ghee, the poison becomes like husk, and of itself forms into a lump.

children.text: iti śuddho hi gandhāśmā nāgajāṃ vikṛtiṃ tyajet ||
children.translated_text: Thus purified, sulfur-stone abandons the alteration caused by <s>nāga</s>.
Otherwise, if drunk without the proper regimen, it would kill like <s>Hālāhala</s> poison.
Sulfur, melted and cast into the juice of <s>bhṛṅga</s>, is purified.
Steamed seven times with those juices, sulfur becomes completely purified.

children.text: sthālyāṃ dugdhaṃ vinikṣipya mukhe vastraṃ nibadhya ca ||
children.translated_text: Having placed milk in a pot and tied cloth over its mouth,
one should put there powdered sulfur, made like sand.
One should cover the sulfur with a broad and long potsherd.
Above the potsherd one should kindle a fire with forest cow-dung cakes and also with cow-dung fuel.
The sulfur, having melted and fallen into the milk, becomes purified.

children.text: itthaṃ viśuddhas triphalājyabhṛṅgamadhvanvitaḥ śāṇamito hi līḍhaḥ
children.translated_text: When purified in this way, mixed with <s>triphala</s>, ghee, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, and honey, and licked in the measure of a <s>śāṇa</s>,
it makes the pair of eyes like those of a vulture and produces long life free from disease.
Sulfur, finely powdered and joined with a sixteenth part of <s>vyoṣa</s>,
should be spread over a cloth one cubit long and then rolled up.
After wrapping it with thread, one should immerse it in oil for one watch.
Holding the wick with tongs, one should then ignite the whole of it.
The melted sulfur will fall drop by drop into a glass vessel.
One should put three drops of that melted substance on a leaf of <s>nāgavallī</s>.

children.text: vallena pramitaṃ śuddhaṃ rasendraṃ ca pramardayet
children.translated_text: Then one should triturate pure <s>rasendra</s> (mercury), measured by a <s>valla</s>,

children.text: aṅgulyātha sapatrāṃ tāṃ drutiṃ sūtaṃ ca bhakṣayet ||
children.translated_text: and with the finger consume that melted sulfur together with the leaf and the mercury.

children.text: karoti dīpanaṃ tīvraṃ kṣayaṃ pāṇḍuṃ ca nāśayet
children.translated_text: It produces strong stimulation of digestion and destroys consumption and pallor.
It also destroys cough, asthma, pain from colic, and very difficult <s>grahaṇī</s> disease.
It quickly destroys undigested matter and produces lightness.
Pure sulfur, melted in an iron vessel smeared with ghee,
and poured with a ladle smeared with ghee, should be taken in the measure of two <s>niṣkas</s>.
It destroys diseases headed by consumption, and skin disease in particular.
Alkalis, sour substances, oils, <s>sauvīra</s>, irritating foods, and pulses
should be avoided during the use of purified sulfur by one who acts for the benefit of the sick.
Sulfur, equal in measure to black pepper and mixed with six times as much <s>triphala</s>,
when rubbed with the root of <s>śampāka</s> and drunk, removes every skin disease.
That root, ground in water, should be applied every day to the body.
This is a preparation whose result has been seen; everywhere its power is unobstructed.
It has been properly proclaimed here by the illustrious <s>Somadeva</s>.
Having drunk sulfur in the measure of two <s>niṣkas</s>, mixed with oil,
then with water of <s>apāmārga</s>, oil, and black pepper,

children.text: vilipya sakalaṃ dehaṃ tiṣṭhed gharme tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: one should smear the whole body and afterwards remain in the heat.

children.text: takrabhaktaṃ ca bhuñjīta tṛtīye prahare khalu
children.translated_text: In the third watch one should eat rice with buttermilk.

children.text: bhajedrātrau tathā vahniṃ samutthāya tataḥ prage ||
children.translated_text: At night one should keep near the fire, and then, rising early in the morning,
after smearing with buffalo dung, one should bathe with cold water.
Then, after anointing the body with ghee, one should bathe with warm wholesome water.
By this sequential procedure there is destroyed with very great speed
stubborn and long-standing scabies and itching, without doubt.
The thousand applications of sulfur have not been stated
because King <s>Somadeva</s> feared making the book too extensive.
<s>Haritāla</s> is said to be of two kinds: the foliated type and the type called lump.

children.text: svarṇavarṇaṃ guru snigdhaṃ tanupatraṃ ca bhāsuram ||
children.translated_text: Golden in color, heavy, unctuous, thin-leaved, and shining,
that is called foliated <s>tālaka</s>, having many leaves and serving as a <s>rasāyana</s>.
The leafless one, resembling a lump, having little essence and also heavy,
takes away women's menstruation; that inferior kind is lump <s>tālaka</s>.
<s>Haritāla</s> is said to remove phlegm, wind, poison, blood disorders, and spirits, and especially women's menstruation.

children.text: snigdham uṣṇakaṭukaṃ ca dīpanaṃ kuṣṭhahāri haritālamucyate ||
children.translated_text: It is unctuous, hot, pungent, digestive-stimulating, and removes skin disease.
Steamed either in water of ash gourd or in water with sesame alkali,
or in water mixed with powders, it is purified by means of a swing apparatus.
Soaked with decoction of horse gram, <s>saubhāgya</s>, buffalo ghee, and curd,
one should place it in a pot and cover it with a luted vessel furnished with holes.
Having properly confined the fire, one should kindle it, increasing it gradually,
for just one watch, after covering the aperture with cow-dung cakes.

children.text: yāmānte chidramudghāṭya dṛṣṭe dhūme ca pāṇḍure
children.translated_text: At the end of the watch, one should open the hole; and when a pale smoke is seen,
one should lift out the cooled vessel, draw out the essence, and take it away.
There are millions of methods for extracting the essences of all stones and minerals;

children.text: granthavistārabhītyā te likhitā na mayā khalu ||
children.translated_text: but through fear of expanding the book, they have certainly not been written by me.
What is everywhere easy to do, readily obtainable, and productive of results,
that alone is stated here concerning <s>rasa</s>, <s>uparasa</s>, and metals.
One should grind <s>pattrālaka</s> for one day with the milky latex of <s>ravi</s>,

children.text: kṣiptvā ṣoḍaśikāṃ taile miśrayitvā tataḥ pacet ||
children.translated_text: put a sixteenth part into oil, mix it, and then cook it.
In an uncovered place, certainly for as long as seven watches,
one should collect the white essence lying below after it has cooled of itself.
Then <s>tālaka</s>, combined with the excrement of a young goat,
should be carefully ground for two days.
Joined with the liquefying group, it should be put into a glass bottle.

children.text: tridhā tāṃ ca mṛdā liptvā pariśoṣya kharātape ||
children.translated_text: Having coated that three times with clay, one should dry it in fierce sunlight.
Then, into the hole of an earthen vessel, one should insert that very bottle halfway,
and kindle the fire for as long as twelve watches.

children.text: kūpīkaṇṭhe sthitaṃ sattvaṃ śubhraṃ śīte samāharet
children.translated_text: When it is cool, one should collect the white essence situated in the neck of the bottle.

children.text: palārdhapramitaṃ tālaṃ baddhvā vastre site dṛḍhe ||
children.translated_text: A half-pala measure of <s>tāla</s> should be tied firmly in a white cloth.
One should carefully smear it with <s>bali</s> and dry it three times.
Into three palas of melted copper one should throw the packet of <s>tālaka</s>.
One should quickly cover it with ash; then one should take the white, soft essence enveloped by copper.
This is stated in the <s>Rasarasāyana</s>.
The clay produced in a mine of <s>Saurāṣṭra</s> is known as <s>tuvarī</s>.
It is smeared on cloths and fixes the dye of madder.
It is proclaimed to be of two kinds, <s>phaṭikā</s> and <s>phullikā</s>.
The slightly yellow, heavy, and unctuous kind is <s>pītikā</s>, a destroyer of poison.
It removes wounds and skin disease, and especially destroys all kinds of skin disease.

children.text: nirbhārā śubhravarṇā ca snigdhā sāmlā parā matā
children.translated_text: The weightless, white-colored, unctuous, and slightly sour one is considered superior.
That is called <s>phulla-tuvarī</s>; by smearing it on, iron acts quickly.

children.text: kāṅkṣī kaṣāyā kaṭukāmlakaṇṭhyā keśyā vraṇaghnī viṣanāśinī ca
children.translated_text: <s>Kāṅkṣī</s> is astringent, pungent, sour, beneficial to the throat and hair, healing to wounds, and destructive of poison.
It removes white leprosy, benefits the eyes, gives pacification of the three doṣas, and digests mercury.
<s>Tuvarī</s>, placed in sour gruel, attains purification after three days.
Triturated with alkalis and acids and heated by blowing, it certainly releases its essence.
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> is said to be threefold: <s>śyāmāṅgī</s>, <s>kaṇavīrikā</s>,
and the one called <s>khaṇḍā</s>; their appearance is distinguished and described.

children.text: śyāmā raktā sagaurā ca bhārāḍhyā śyāmikā matā
children.translated_text: The dark-red one with a pale tinge and rich in weight is considered <s>śyāmikā</s>.
The lustrous, non-pale, copper-colored one is <s>kaṇavīrikā</s>.
The powdery one, very red-bodied and heavy, is the variety beginning with the name <s>khaṇḍa</s>.
Each succeeding one is proclaimed better than the preceding, rich in essence.
<s>Manaḥśilā</s>, foremost among all <s>rasāyana</s> substances, is bitter, pungent, hot, and destructive of kapha and vāta.
It is essence-bearing, and removes poisons from beings, weak digestion, itching, urticaria, and wasting.
Impregnated seven times with the juice of <s>Agastya</s> leaves,
or with ginger juices, <s>manaḥśilā</s> is purified.
With one eighth part of slag, molasses, guggulu, and ghee,

children.text: koṣṭhyāṃ ruddhvā dṛḍhaṃ dhmātā sattvaṃ muñcenmanaḥśilā ||
children.translated_text: sealed tightly in a furnace and heated by blowing, <s>manaḥśilā</s> releases its essence.
With <s>bhūnāga</s>, washed <s>saubhāgya</s>, and <s>madana</s> thoroughly triturated,
one should make a crucible with the water of bitter-gourd leaves and place it there.
One should then blow upon <s>śilā</s> ground with alkali and acid.
When heated by blowing for just two ghaṭikās, it gives up its essence.
<s>Sauvīra</s> is said to be an <s>añjana</s>; next is <s>rasāñjana</s>.
<s>Sroto'ñjana</s> is another, and so also <s>puṣpāñjana</s>;

children.text: nīlāñjanaṃ hi teṣāṃ ca svarūpamiha varṇyate ||
children.translated_text: and among them there is <s>nīlāñjana</s>. Their appearance is described here.
<s>Sauvīramañjana</s> is smoky, removes disorders of blood and pitta, and is cooling.
It destroys vomiting, hiccup, and eye disease, and cleanses and heals wounds.
<s>Rasāñjana</s> has a yellowish appearance and removes poison and blood disease.
It removes asthma and hiccup, improves complexion, and destroys disorders of vāta, pitta, and blood.

children.text: sroto'ñjanaṃ himaṃ snigdhaṃ kaṣāyaṃ svādu lekhanam
children.translated_text: <s>Sroto'ñjana</s> is cooling, unctuous, astringent, sweet, and scraping.
It benefits the eyes and suppresses aggravation of hiccup, poison, vomiting, kapha, pitta, and blood.
<s>Puṣpāñjana</s> is white, unctuous, cooling, and removes all eye diseases.
It destroys extremely obstinate hiccup and removes poison, fever, and disease.
<s>Nīlāñjana</s> is heavy, unctuous, beneficial to the eyes, and removes the three doṣas.
It is a <s>rasāyana</s>, acts against gold, and makes iron soft.
The <s>añjana</s> substances are purified by the juices of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> leaves.
One should collect the essence of the <s>añjana</s> substances in the same way as the essence of <s>manohvā</s>.
On the slopes and peaks of <s>Himavat</s>, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> arises.
Of that, one kind is called <s>nalikā</s>, and the other is considered <s>reṇuka</s>.
The first <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, yellow in luster, heavy, and unctuous, is the best.

children.text: śyāmaṃ pītaṃ laghu tyaktasattvaṃ neṣṭaṃ hi reṇukam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>reṇuka</s> kind, dark-yellow, light, and lacking essence, is not desired.
Some say that <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is the excrement of a newly born elephant.
That, blackish-yellow in appearance, is described as purgative.
Some say that the stalk of <s>tejivāha</s> plants is called <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>.
They say that the white-yellowish one is an exceedingly strong purgative.
In <s>rasa</s> and <s>rasāyana</s> it is best, though without essence and much altered.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is bitter and pungent, hot in potency, and strongly purgative.
It removes wounds, upward-moving wind, pain, distress, abdominal tumors, spleen disease, and rectal pain.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> becomes purified when it has been infused three times with excellent water.

children.text: sattvākarṣo'sya na prokto yasmātsattvamayaṃ hi tat
children.translated_text: The extraction of its essence has not been taught, because that substance is itself made of essence.
For the purpose of purgation, one should take it with absorbent substances in a barley-grain measure.
After purging, it destroys the filling up of <s>āma</s> in only a moment.
Eaten together with betel leaves, it should quickly purge and remove the disorder.
A decoction of <s>Barbūrī</s> root, with equal parts cumin and <s>saubhāgya</s>,
should be drunk by a man again and again to destroy <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> poisoning.
<s>Kāsīsa</s> is of one kind beginning with <s>Vālukā</s>, and another beginning with <s>Puṣpa</s>.
It is alkaline and sour, heavy, smoke-colored, somewhat hot in potency, and antidotal to poison.
<s>Vālukāpūrva-kāsīsa</s> removes white leprosy and dyes the hair.
<s>Puṣpādi-kāsīsa</s> is very famous, somewhat hot, astringent and sour, and exceedingly beneficial for the eyes.
It destroys poison, disorders of wind and phlegm, wounds, white leprosy, wasting disease, and also dyes the hair.

children.text: sakṛd bhṛṅgāmbunā klinnaṃ kāsīsaṃ nirmalaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: <s>Kāsīsa</s>, moistened once with <s>bhṛṅga</s> water, becomes stainless.
Its essence too should be extracted in the same way as the essence of <s>tuvarī</s>.
Strong calcined <s>kāsīsa</s> and <s>kānta</s> killed with <s>kāsīsa</s>,
both in equal parts and combined with <s>triphala</s> and <s>vella</s>,
soaked in ghee and honey in uneven portions, should be taken in the morning in a <s>śāṇa</s> measure.
It quickly destroys white leprosy, pallor, and wasting diseases.
It entirely removes abdominal tumors, spleen disease, pain, and urinary disorders.
When used according to the <s>rasāyana</s> regimen for up to a year,
it is excellent for drying up <s>āma</s> and for kindling weak digestive fire.
It certainly destroys gray hair together with wrinkles.
One kind is <s>pāṣāṇagairika</s>, and the second is <s>svarṇagairika</s>.
<s>Pāṣāṇagairika</s> is said to be hard and copper-colored.

children.text: svādu snigdhaṃ himaṃ netryaṃ kaṣāyaṃ raktapittanut ||
children.translated_text: It is sweet, unctuous, cooling, good for the eyes, astringent, and removes bleeding and pitta.
<s>Svarṇagairika</s> destroys hiccup, vomiting, and poison, and removes blood disorders.
The other <s>pāṣāṇagairika</s> has fewer qualities than the former.

children.text: gairikaṃ hi gavāṃ dugdhairbhāvitaṃ śuddhim ṛcchati
children.translated_text: <s>Gairika</s> attains purification when it is infused with the milk of cows.
<s>Gairika</s> is indeed essence in form; so it has been declared by <s>Nandin</s>.
Some say that essence falls from <s>gairika</s> steamed with alkaline and sour substances.
It attends upon lord mercury and enters into a more excellent union of qualities.
<s>Kampilla</s>, another <s>Gaurīpāṣāṇa</s>, <s>Navasāraka</s>,
<s>Kaparda</s>, <s>Vahnijāra</s>, <s>Girisindūra</s>, and <s>Hiṅgula</s>,
and <s>Boddāraśṛṅga</s>: these eight are regarded as common minerals.
They are said by authorities beginning with <s>Nāgārjuna</s> to bring success in mercury.
It resembles brick powder, is rich in luster, and is purgative.
Born in the country of <s>Saurāṣṭra</s>, that is considered <s>kampillaka</s>.
<s>Kampillaka</s> removes pitta, wounds, bloating, and constipation, and is an enemy to phlegm, abdominal disease, worms, and abdominal tumors.
<s>Kampillaka</s> removes rectal disease, <s>āma</s>, colic, fever, and swelling, and takes away diseases requiring purgation.
<s>Gaurīpāṣāṇaka</s> is yellow, irregular, and reduced to powder when calcined.
It binds mercury, is unctuous, removes the humors, and produces potency in mercury.
When the woods of <s>karīra</s> and <s>pīlu</s> are being cooked, it arises from them.
That alkali is <s>navasāra</s>, called <s>cūlikā-lavaṇa</s>.
The pale, light salt produced in the burning of bricks
is called <s>navasāra</s>; it is also that <s>cūlikā-lavaṇa</s>.
It digests lord mercury, melts metals, and produces gastric fire.
It removes abdominal tumors, spleen disease, and dryness of the mouth, and digests eaten meat and the like.
Also called <s>viḍa</s>, it removes the three humors; it is considered <s>cūlikā-lavaṇa</s>.
The best <s>varāṭikā</s> is yellowish, nodular on the back, and long-stalked.
It is designated by rasa physicians with the name <s>carācara</s>.
One weighing one and a half <s>niṣkas</s> is best; one of a <s>niṣka</s> weight is middling.
One weighing a quarter less than a <s>niṣka</s> is declared lowest.
It removes pain beginning with that from digestion and destroys <s>grahaṇī</s> disease and wasting.
It is pungent, hot, kindling, aphrodisiac, good for the eyes, and removes wind and phlegm.
It is taught for the digestion of lord mercury and is praised among the substances of <s>biḍa</s>.

children.text: tadanye tu varāṭāḥ syur guravaḥ śleṣmapittalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Other cowries are heavy and increase phlegm and pitta.

children.text: hatvā hatvā guṇān bhūyo vikārān kurvate na hi
children.translated_text: When they have been repeatedly killed, they do not afterward produce disorders of their qualities.
Cowries steamed in sour gruel for a watch of the day attain purification.
The afterbirth of the fire-crocodile, cast out by the ocean,
and dried by the heat of the sun, is remembered as <s>agnijāra</s>.
Because it is purified by oceanic alkali, purification is not required for it.
<s>Agnijāra</s> removes the three humors and dispels tetanus and other wind disorders.
It increases the potency of mercury, kindles digestion, and also performs digestion or calcination.
In great mountains, a small amount of mineral essence situated inside stone,
dry and red, is designated by the name <s>rasasindūra</s>.
<s>Girisindūra</s> pacifies the three humors, is purgative, and is foremost for binding mercury.
It makes the body and metals firm, is good for the eyes, and is called <s>girisindūra</s>.
<s>Hiṅgula</s> is known as <s>śukatuṇḍa</s>; another is <s>haṃsapāka</s>.
Among them the first has few qualities and is called <s>carmāra</s>.
That which has white streaks and resembles coral is called <s>haṃsapāka</s>.
<s>Hiṅgula</s> removes all humors, kindles digestion, and is an excellent <s>rasāyana</s>.
It removes all diseases, is aphrodisiac, and is highly praised for digestion of mercury.
Mercury obtained from this is equal in qualities to digested sulfur.
Having been infused seven times with ginger juices or with the water of <s>lakuca</s>,

children.text: śoṣito bhāvayitvā ca nirdoṣo jāyate khalu ||
children.translated_text: and dried after being thus treated, it truly becomes free from faults.
It has leaves and is yellow in color; in the <s>Gurjara</s> region,
on the side of Mount <s>Arbuda</s>, grows <s>boddāraśṛṅgaka</s>.
The <s>sattva</s> of lead pacifies wind and phlegm and removes diseases of men;
it is excellent for binding <s>rasa</s> (mercury) and supreme for dyeing the hair.
All ordinary minerals, with the liquid juice of <s>mātuluṅga</s> (citron),
when treated three times and dried, become free from defects.

children.text: yāni kāni ca sattvāni tāni śudhyantyaśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>sattvas</s> there are, they are purified completely;
when smelted with the purifying group, they unite with one another.

children.text: māṇikyamuktāphalavidrumāṇi tārkṣyaṃ ca puṣpaṃ bhiduraṃ ca nīlam
children.translated_text: Ruby, pearl, coral, <s>tārkṣya</s>, <s>puṣpa</s>, diamond, sapphire,

children.text: gomedakaṃ cātha vidūrakaṃ ca krameṇa ratnāni navagrahāṇām ||
children.translated_text: <s>gomedaka</s>, and <s>vidūraka</s>: these, in order, are the gems of the nine planets.
According to the friendship of the planets, <s>kuruvinda</s>, <s>puṣpa</s>, coral, pearl, <s>tārkṣya</s>, diamond,
the stone called sapphire, <s>gomedaka</s>, and <s>vidūraka</s> are to be worn in rings, in order, for the desired success.

children.text: rase rasāyane dāne dhāraṇe ca devatārcane
children.translated_text: In work with <s>rasa</s>, in rasāyana, in gifts, in wearing them, and in worship of deities,
well-marked and well-born gems are prescribed for accomplishment.
Ruby is called <s>padmarāga</s>; a second kind is <s>nīlagandhi</s>.

children.text: śītaṃ kuśeśayacchāyaṃ svacchaṃ snigdhaṃ guru sphuṭam ||
children.translated_text: It is cool, like the shade of a lotus, clear, smooth, heavy, and bright.
Round or oblong, with even body, such a ruby is said to be the best.
The blue one, born from the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, with a blue core and red luster,
excellent like the former ruby, is that ruby called <s>nīlagandhi</s>.
A ruby marked by holes, roughness, dirtiness, dryness, and pallor,

children.text: cipiṭaṃ laghu vakraṃ ca māṇikyaṃ duṣṭam aṣṭadhā ||
children.translated_text: flat, light, and crooked is defective in eight ways.
Ruby kindles digestion, is aphrodisiac, and removes disorders of phlegm, wind, wasting, and pain;
it destroys spirits, <s>vetālas</s>, evil, and diseases born of karma.

children.text: hlādi śvetaṃ laghu snigdhaṃ raśmivannirmalaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Pleasing, white, light, smooth, radiant, spotless, and large,

children.text: khyātaṃ toyaprabhaṃ vṛttaṃ mauktikaṃ navadhā śubham ||
children.translated_text: known for a watery shine and round form: a pearl is auspicious in nine ways.
A pearl with a rough body, without moisture, dark, coppery, resembling salt,

children.text: ardhaśubhraṃ ca vikaṭaṃ granthilaṃ mauktikaṃ tyajet ||
children.translated_text: half-white, misshapen, or knotted should be rejected.
Pearl is regarded as destroying phlegm, bile, and wasting, and as removing cough, dyspnea, and weak digestion;
it gives nourishment, is aphrodisiac and life-promoting, and removes burning.
Coral, with the color of a ripe <s>bimba</s> fruit, round or oblong and not crooked,

children.text: snigdham avraṇakaṃ sthūlaṃ pravālaṃ saptadhā matam ||
children.translated_text: smooth, uninjured, and large, is regarded as having seven qualities.
Coral that is pale, gray, rough, wounded, furnished with hollows,
without weight, or white in color is not desired in eight ways.
Coral destroys wasting, bile, blood disorders, and cough; it kindles digestion, digests, and is light.
<s>Vidruma</s> pacifies poison, spirits, and the like, and removes eye diseases.
<s>Tārkṣya</s>, green-yellow in color, heavy, smooth, auspicious, with a flashing mass of rays,

children.text: masṛṇaṃ bhāsuraṃ tārkṣyaṃ gātraṃ saptaguṇaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: smooth and shining in body, is considered to have seven qualities.

children.text: kapiśaṃ karkaśaṃ nīlaṃ pāṇḍu kṛṣṇaṃ salāghavam
children.translated_text: <s>Tārkṣya</s> that is tawny, rough, blue, pale, black, light,

children.text: cipiṭaṃ vikaṭaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ rūkṣaṃ tārkṣyaṃ na śasyate ||
children.translated_text: flat, misshapen, dark, or dry is not praised.
<s>Tārkṣya</s> removes fever, vomiting, poison, dyspnea, combined derangement of the humors, and weak digestion;
it destroys piles, anemia, and swelling, and increases vital strength.

children.text: puṣparāgaṃ guru snigdhaṃ svacchaṃ sthūlaṃ samaṃ mṛdu
children.translated_text: <s>Puṣparāga</s> that is heavy, smooth, clear, large, even, and soft,
like a <s>karṇikāra</s> blossom, smooth and auspicious, is eightfold in quality.

children.text: niṣprabhaṃ karkaśaṃ rūkṣaṃ pītaṃ śyāmaṃ natonnatam
children.translated_text: One should reject <s>puṣparāga</s> that is lusterless, rough, dry, yellow, dark, unevenly high and low,
brownish, tawny, or pale.
<s>Puṣparāga</s> removes poison, vomiting, phlegm, wind, and weak digestion;
it pacifies burning and skin disease, kindles digestion, is light, and promotes digestion.

children.text: vajraṃ ca trividhaṃ proktaṃ naro nārī napuṃsakam
children.translated_text: Diamond is said to be of three kinds: male, female, and neuter.
Each earlier one is better than the following in <s>rasa</s>, potency, and post-digestive effect.
Eight-edged, eight-faceted, six-angled, and exceedingly brilliant,
with the appearance of cloud, rainbow, or water: this is called a male diamond.
The same, but flat in form, is a female diamond, round or oblong;
round, with blunt angular tips and somewhat heavy, is neuter.
A female, male, or neuter diamond should be applied respectively for a woman, a man, or one of neuter sex;
through reversal it does not give fruit anywhere, except in the case of a male diamond.
By the distinction of white and other colors, each of these is fourfold:
<s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>kṣatriya</s>, <s>vaiśya</s>, and <s>śūdra</s>, each giving the result proper to its own color-class.
A color that is superior or most superior gives result even for a lower color-class;
this rule was stated by <s>Bhairava</s> for all substances whatsoever.

children.text: āyuṣpradaṃ jhaṭiti sadguṇadaṃ ca vṛṣyaṃ doṣatrayapraśamanaṃ sakalāmayaghnam
children.translated_text: Diamond grants long life at once, gives good qualities, is aphrodisiac, pacifies the three humors, and destroys all disease;

children.text: sūtendrabandhavadhasadguṇakṛt pradīpi mṛtyuṃ jayed amṛtopamayeva vajram ||
children.translated_text: it effects the binding, killing, and good qualities of chief mercury, kindles, and conquers death, as if it were like nectar.
<s>Grāsa</s>, <s>trāsa</s>, <s>bindu</s>, <s>rekhā</s>, and water-in-the-core:
these five are considered common defects in all gems.

children.text: kṣetratoyabhavā doṣā ratneṣu na laganti ca
children.translated_text: Defects born of the field and water do not cling to gems;

children.text: bhairavastu punaḥ prāha doṣo doṣe'sti sarvathā ||
children.translated_text: but <s>Bhairava</s> again said, 'A defect is always a defect.'
A diamond, boiled in a decoction of <s>kulattha</s> or in boiled <s>kodrava</s>,
boiled for the span of one <s>yāma</s>, is certainly purified.
A diamond treated four times with the blood of bedbugs,
and wrapped with pellets made from the flesh of the fragrant musk-rat,
should then be heated thirty times with <s>puṭas</s> called <s>varāha</s>.

children.text: dhmātvā dhmātvā śataṃ vārān kulatthakvāthake kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: After that, having heated it again and again one hundred times, one should throw it into a decoction of <s>kulattha</s>.
Others say that this procedural sequence should be performed one hundred times.
with <s>śilā</s> (mineral stone) ground in <s>lakuca</s> juice mixed with a decoction of <s>kulattha</s>,

children.text: śilayā liptamūṣāyāṃ vajraṃ kṣiptvā nirudhya ca
children.translated_text: one should smear the crucible with that, place the diamond inside, and seal it.
One should heat it properly eight times in a <s>puṭa</s> with thoroughly dried forest cow-dung cakes.
Then, after blowing it a hundred times, when it is placed in purified mercury,

children.text: niścitaṃ mriyate vajraṃ bhasma vāritaraṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: the diamond certainly dies; its ash becomes able to float on water.
Truth-speaking <s>Somasenānī</s> declared this killing of diamond,
and, as an enthusiast for <s>rasa</s> (alchemy), spoke it together with tested proof.
Smeared with the blood of bedbugs and dried seven times,
and placed in an iron vessel filled with the juice of <s>kāsamarda</s>,
when it has been heated all around seven times, it certainly becomes diamond ash.
This procedure was proclaimed by the great sage <s>Brahmajyotis</s>.
Ground in the bulb of the <s>nīlajyotis</s> creeper and dried in the sun's heat,
diamond reaches the state of ash, like karma through the fire of knowledge.
With earthworms made into paste by means of the juice produced from the fruit of <s>madana</s>,
one should smear it and heat it in a <s>puṭa</s> twenty times.
Then, after powdering that diamond, it should be mixed with a little <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax).
One should certainly melt it with a twentieth part of the essence of <s>kharabhūnāga</s>.
Heated with an equal amount of gold, it is to be used in preparations beginning with mercury.
Triturated with three times as much mercury and made into a pill,
when kept in the mouth it quickly fastens loose teeth.

children.text: triṃśadbhāgamitaṃ hi vajrabhasitaṃ svarṇaṃ kalābhāgikaṃ tāraṃ cāṣṭaguṇaṃ śivāmṛtavaraṃ rudrāṃśakaṃ cābhrakam
children.translated_text: Diamond ash should indeed measure thirty parts, gold one <s>kalā</s> part, silver eightfold, the excellent <s>śivāmṛta</s> one <s>Rudra</s> share, and mica

children.text: pādāṃśaṃ khalu tāpyakaṃ vasuguṇaṃ vaikrāntakaṃ ṣaḍguṇaṃ bhāgo'pyuktarasādraso'yamuditaḥ ṣāḍguṇyasaṃsiddhaye ||
children.translated_text: one quarter share, <s>tāpyaka</s> eightfold, <s>vaikrāntaka</s> sixfold, and one part of the stated mercury; this preparation is said to accomplish sixfold potency.
There are <s>jalanīla</s>, <s>indranīla</s>, and <s>śakranīla</s>; among them <s>śakranīla</s> is the best.
That which has a blue appearance containing whiteness and is light is <s>jalanīlaka</s>.
That which has a blue appearance containing blackness and is heavy is <s>śakranīlaka</s>.
Of one color, heavy, smooth, clear, and compact in form,
soft, with a light shining in the middle: in these seven ways <s>nīla</s> (blue sapphire) is excellent.

children.text: komalaṃ vihitaṃ varṇaṃ nirbhāraṃ raktagandhi ca
children.translated_text: Soft, with its color properly formed, without weight, and with a red scent or tinge,

children.text: cipiṭābhaṃ sarūkṣaṃ ca jalanīlaṃ ca saptadhā ||
children.translated_text: flat in appearance and rough: <s>jalanīla</s> is of seven such kinds.
<s>Nīla</s> is said to remove cough and dyspnea, to be aphrodisiac, to destroy the three humors, and to kindle digestion well.
It removes irregular fever, bad skin disease, and sin.
Because it has a similar color, the gem is called <s>gomeda</s>.
Very clear, with the hue of cow's liquid, clear, smooth, even, and heavy,
free from cracks, polished, and shining: <s>gomeda</s> is praised in eight ways.
Colorless, light, rough-bodied, flat, and covered with a film,
lustreless and like yellow glass: such <s>gomeda</s> does not bring good fortune.
<s>Gomeda</s> destroys phlegm and pitta and removes consumption and pallor.
It kindles digestion, digests, is appetizing, is good for the skin, and awakens intelligence.

children.text: vaiḍūryaṃ śyāmaśubhrābhaṃ samaṃ svacchaṃ guru sphuṭam
children.translated_text: <s>Vaiḍūrya</s> (cat's-eye) has a dark and white appearance; it is even, clear, heavy, and distinct.
When it contains a moving white upper streak, it is said to be auspicious.
Dark, with a hue like water, flat, light, and rough,
and containing a red upper streak: such <s>vaiḍūrya</s> is not praised.
<s>Vaiḍūrya</s> destroys bleeding disorders and increases wisdom, life, and strength.
It removes diseases dominated by pitta, kindles digestion, and loosens the stool.
Ruby is purified with sour liquid, and pearl likewise with <s>jayantī</s>.
Coral is purified with the group of alkalis, and <s>tārkṣya</s> likewise with cow's milk.
<s>Puṣparāga</s> is purified with sour grain-gruels mixed with <s>kulattha</s> decoction,
diamond with waters of <s>taṇḍulīya</s>, and <s>nīla</s> with the juice of <s>nīlī</s>.
<s>Gomeda</s> is purified with <s>rocanā</s>, and <s>vaiḍūrya</s> with water of <s>triphalā</s>.
With <s>śilā</s>, sulfur, and <s>tālaka</s> ground in <s>lakuca</s> juice,
gems other than diamond are indeed killed by eight <s>puṭas</s>.
<s>Rāmaṭha</s>, the five salts, and the three alkalis,
<s>māṃsadrāvī</s>, sour <s>vetasa</s>, and <s>cūlikā</s> salt,
the ripe fruit of <s>sthalakumbhī</s>, and likewise auspicious <s>jvālāmukhī</s>,

children.text: dravantī ca rudantī ca payasyā citramūlakam ||
children.translated_text: <s>dravantī</s>, <s>rudantī</s>, <s>payasyā</s>, and <s>citramūlaka</s>,
the milk of <s>snuhī</s> and also of <s>arka</s>: all this should be carefully pounded together.
After making a ball, one should then place them in its middle.
The gems should be endowed with good qualities, genuine in kind, and auspicious.

children.text: bhūrje taṃ golakaṃ kṛtvā sūtreṇāveṣṭya yatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having made that into a ball in birch-bark, one should wrap it carefully with thread.
Again wrapping it with cloth and placing it in a swinging apparatus,
inside a pot filled with a fermented preparation joined with all sour substances,
one should steam it for three days and nights with an intense fire.
Taking it out from there and washing it, one obtains the liquefaction born from gems.
It has a lustre equal to the gems, is light, auspicious, and makes body and metals.

children.text: durmelā rasarājena naikatvaṃ yāti tena sā ||
children.translated_text: It is hard to combine with the king of mercury; therefore it does not become one with him.
With the group beginning with <s>rāmaṭha</s> it mixes; there is no doubt.

children.text: suprasanne mahādeve drutiḥ kasya na sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Mahādeva</s> is highly gracious, whose liquefaction would not succeed?
Devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s> is rare, and the binding of mercury is rare.
Here in the world, this gem-liquefaction is rare among men of little fortune.

The wearing of gems is declared to remove the restraint and affliction of planets beginning with the sun, to give long life and health, to bestow the rise of good fortune, luck, mastery, wealth, and energy, and to produce courage.

children.text: duḥchāyāṃcaladhūlisaṅgatibhavālakṣmīharaṃ sarvadā ratnānāṃ paridhāraṇaṃ nigaditaṃ bhūtādinirṇāśanam ||
children.translated_text: It is said always to remove misfortune arising from bad shadow and contact with shifting dust, and to destroy spirits and the like.
The moon-like <s>Soma</s>, foremost among the good, spoke of the complete collection of qualities of jewels;
a virtuous man does not declare a good jewel to be what is not furnished with qualities.
A jewel endowed with the marks of color and proper kind gives results
in mercury work, in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation), in gifting, and in wearing, each in its own different way.
One <s>karṣa</s> of auspicious ash of ruby, possessing good origin and qualities,
and the ashes of gold, mica, copper, and magnetite, each separately,
increased threefold, should be triturated with equal sulfur.
It should be heated carefully five times with forest fuel-cakes.
In the same way it should be heated with <s>śilā</s> and lac, and also with blue antimony.
A fine <s>kajjalī</s> should be prepared with equal sulfur, stone, and mercury.
Then, carefully taking that <s>kajjalī</s>, immediately afterward
one should melt it in an iron vessel with a small fire of jujube wood.
The ashes beginning with ruby should be placed there and thoroughly mixed.
Then that <s>kajjalī</s> should be triturated with ginger juices.
When properly dried, it should be powdered and placed in a pleasing small container.
This <s>rasāyana</s> beginning with ruby is to be combined with <s>vyoṣa</s> and ghee.
Licked together with <s>vyoṣa</s> and ghee for six months by one who eats wholesome food,
it destroys all diseases, along with old age and grey hair.
Taking food three times, he lives a hundred years;
it destroys all illnesses beginning with wasting, according to the respective disease and vehicle.
Pearl, triturated in the juice of <s>jayantī</s> and killed with <s>śukapiccha</s>,
should be in the measure of mercury, and ash of gold should be twice as much.
Ash produced from magnetite should be three times as much, and essence of mica four times as much.
After adding the auspicious sulfur and treating it with ginger,
one should heat it twenty times, melt it, and strain it through cloth.
A <s>kajjalī</s> should be made with strong mercury equal in weight to all of it.
Having melted it as before, one should throw in the ashes of pearl and the rest.
After mixing it, one should place in it milk produced from a she-goat.
When it has been dried, it should be powdered and put into a glass bottle.
Taken with long pepper and honey in the measure of a <s>valla</s>,
by the rule for <s>rasāyana</s>, within a year it makes a person
free from wrinkles and grey hair and rid of old age.
He has full hearing, teeth, and the rest, is long-lived for a hundred years, and has sight;
he is endowed with the strength of a rutting elephant and is furnished with victory in disputes.
Licked with honey, ghee, and oil, and with <s>aśvagandhā</s> accompanied by <s>kaṇā</s>,
it certainly destroys wasting disease in half a <s>maṇḍala</s>.
With the respective vehicles for the respective diseases, it destroys all illnesses.
It gives sons to barren women and destroys diseases of women in childbed.
It is supremely wholesome for children, aphrodisiac, and most excellent for longevity.

children.text: nāgodaropaviṣṭaṃ ca hanti strīṇāṃ ca vegataḥ ||
children.translated_text: It also swiftly destroys <s>nāgodara</s> and disorders lodged in the wombs of women.
Combined with fresh butter and combined with <s>tavarāja</s>,
it is proclaimed to be praised in all diseases of pregnant women.
Four <s>palas</s> of coral ash and dead silver,
the same amount, twice as much copper, and pyrite half as much as the coral,
diamond in a thirtieth part and blue stone in a sixteenth part,
essence of mica equal to all, and <s>tālaka</s> equal in every respect:
one should triturate these with citron water for four days.
With purified mercury amounting to half of all that, and with sulfur twice as much as that,

children.text: vihitāṃ kajjalīṃ samyak drāvayitvā yathā purā
children.translated_text: one should properly prepare a <s>kajjalī</s> and melt it as before.
After placing in the ashes beginning with coral and mixing them,
one should properly quench it in cow ghee that is twelve years old.
Having sealed it in a covered pair of saucers smeared with ghee, one should steam it slowly.
After powdering it, one should treat it seven times with the juices of <s>bhṛṅga</s>.
Together with <s>vyoṣa</s> and ghee, it destroys <s>jūrti</s> disease in three days.
It destroys wasting in half a <s>maṇḍala</s>, and <s>grahaṇī</s>, anemia, and jaundice,
the disease called <s>kumbhakāmalikā</s>, upward movement of wind, and great abdominal swelling.
It destroys diabetes, increase of fat, wind disease, and phlegmatic illness,
rectal disease, weak digestion, and urinary wind entirely.
It destroys diseases born from the house of love, infertility disorders, and skin diseases.
The vehicles are, in every case, <s>vyoṣa</s>, ghee, and water of <s>citraka</s>.

children.text: bhūyo bhūyo visūcyartir dehino yasya jāyate
children.translated_text: For a person in whom the pain of <s>visūcī</s> arises again and again,

children.text: raso'yaṃ tasya dātavyo maṇḍalānāṃ trayaṃ khalu
children.translated_text: this mercury preparation should be given for three <s>maṇḍalas</s> indeed.
In <s>āma</s> disease it should also be given by physicians for as long as a year.
One <s>śāṇa</s> of ash of <s>tārkṣya</s>, and half as much diamond ash,
and two <s>niṣkas</s> each of killed gold, <s>arka</s>, and magnetite:
iron ash and killed mercury should all be triturated together.
It should be heated twenty times with heatings called <s>kukkuṭa</s>.
Together with <s>śilā</s>, sulfur, and <s>tālaka</s> mixed with the water of <s>amṛtā</s>,

children.text: saptavāraṃ dravaiḥ sārdhaṃ daśabhiḥ piṣṭakaiḥ puṭet ||
children.translated_text: one should heat it seven times with liquids and ten fuel-cakes.

children.text: evaṃ siddhaṃ prabhāvāḍhyaṃ tārkṣyaṃ nāma rasāyanam
children.translated_text: When thus perfected, this powerful <s>rasāyana</s> is named <s>Tārkṣya</s>.
Drunk in a dose measured by a mustard seed, accompanied by the juices of <s>citraka</s> and ginger,
it cures all diseases born from the three <s>doṣas</s>, and those arising from phlegm and wind as well,
even those incurable for all physicians and by tens of millions of medicines.
It produces excessive hunger and digests what has been eaten in an instant.
A fine ash produced from <s>puṣparāga</s>, measured at half a <s>pala</s>,
and half of that amount of yellow glass, and half of that amount of copper ash,
and silver amounting to half of the copper, and gold half as much as that.
Take ash of <s>vajra</s> (diamond), half that quantity, and calcined <s>abhraka</s> (mica) equal to the whole.

children.text: tatsamaṃ sūryakāntaṃ ca māritaṃ balinā saha
children.translated_text: Also take <s>sūryakānta</s> equal to that, killed together with <s>balin</s>.

children.text: tulyena balinā sārdhaṃ daśavāraṃ puṭet khalu ||
children.translated_text: Together with an equal quantity of <s>balin</s>, it should indeed be fired ten times.
There should also be those separate firings of <s>nīlāñjana</s>, <s>ala</s>, and <s>tāpya</s>.
Thus this accomplished preparation is called the <s>puṣparāga-rasāyana</s>.
It destroys all diseases beginning with wasting and is supreme for removing disorders of leprosy and skin disease.
It calms pain from rectal growths and abdominal tumors, produces sons, and is an excellent aphrodisiac.

children.text: rasāyanaṃ tathā caitat kṣipraṃ gulmaharaṃ striyāḥ
children.translated_text: This too is a <s>rasāyana</s>; for a woman it quickly removes abdominal tumors.
It is declared to be a supreme kindler of digestion and destroys jaundice and anemia.
Why say much here? It destroys every disease.
Take one <s>karṣa</s> of killed <s>vajra</s>, and the same amount of essence of <s>bhūnāga</s>.
Then take twice as much gold, and essence of <s>kha</s> equal to the gold.

children.text: tāvanmātraṃ ca kāntāyaḥ sarvaṃ vāritaraṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Take the same amount of magnetic iron, all made to float on water.
Mercury is stated to be one eighth in relation to all these ingredients.
<s>Śukapiccha</s>, equal to all of them, should be triturated with sour preparations of chickpea.
After making a fine ball, one should dry it in the shade.

children.text: tato bhūnāgasattvaṃ hi gandhakena samaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: Then the essence of <s>bhūnāga</s> should be added with an equal amount of sulfur.
It is to be fired a hundred times, and a hundred times with <s>tāpya</s> substances.
Then it is treated twenty times with <s>sūryaparṇī</s> leaves or with milks.
It is covered with powder of <s>bhūnāga</s> along with <s>guñjā</s>, borax, and wax.

children.text: vartayitvā tu taṃ golaṃ kalkenānena lepayet
children.translated_text: Having rolled that ball, one should smear it with this paste.
Then, with a layer half a finger thick, after drying it in harsh sunlight,
one should place it in a sand apparatus and cook it for five days.
Then, with the milks of <s>trikoṇa-gaṇḍīra</s> mixed with sulfur,

children.text: mardayitvā tu taṃ golaṃ puṭedvārāṇi viṃśatim
children.translated_text: having triturated that ball, one should fire it twenty times.
Then, after making it into fine cloth-sifted powder, one should put it inside a casket.
One should take this excellent <s>vajra-rasāyana</s> in a dose the size of a <s>guñjā</s>.
For all diseases, known and unknown, and for diseases of many kinds,
the physician should indeed give it with the vehicle appropriate to each particular disease.

children.text: na so'sti rogo loke'sminyo hyanena na śāmyati ||
children.translated_text: There is no disease in this world that is not pacified by this.
When taken as a <s>rasāyana</s> for three <s>maṇḍalas</s>,
it surely produces bodily perfection, causing wonder in the whole world.
Except for <s>bilva</s>, everything is prescribed here as suitable diet.
Take ash made from blue gem, one <s>pala</s> in measure, and diamond,

children.text: svarṇaṃ raupyaṃ ca kāntaṃ ca tāpyakaṃ nṛpavartakam ||
children.translated_text: gold, silver, magnetic iron, <s>tāpya</s>, and <s>nṛpavartaka</s>.

children.text: samāṃśaṃ sarvametat syāt sarvatulyaṃ ca śulvakam
children.translated_text: All this should be in equal parts, and copper should be equal to the whole.
All this should be taken in killed form and combined with an equal amount of sulfur.
One should triturate it with <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil until eight days have passed.
Having placed sulfur above and below it, one should fire it twenty times.
Afterward one should infuse it seven times with juices of white <s>muṇḍī</s>.
Thus this accomplished, power-filled, excellent preparation is the <s>nīla-rasāyana</s>.
Taken in a dose the size of a <s>guñjā</s>, it destroys all diseases.

children.text: jvaraṃ pāṇḍuṃ kṣayaṃ kāsaṃ śūlamarśaśca gulmakam ||
children.translated_text: It destroys fever, anemia, wasting, cough, colic, piles, and abdominal tumors,

children.text: udaraṃ kuṣṭharogaṃ ca śvāsaṃ pañcavidhaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: abdominal disease, leprosy and skin disease, and also the five kinds of dyspnea.
With the corresponding medicinal combination it removes each corresponding disease.
<s>Gomeda</s>, combined with sulfur and joined with the liquid of <s>lakuca</s>,
when fired ten times, becomes ash measuring one <s>pala</s>.
Gold, silver, and magnetic iron are all killed by medicinal substances.
A <s>krāmaṇa</s> agent, in quarter portions, is soaked with <s>cūlikā</s> water.
<s>Tāpya</s>, fired ten times with <s>gandharva</s> oil,
becomes non-rising ash, in every way rich in qualities.
Into melted <s>kajjalī</s> made with half as much mercury and sulfur,
one should put the three previous ashes, mix them thoroughly, and collect the mixture.
Having pulverized it, one should infuse it seven times with liquids of <s>muṇḍikā</s>.
Then, after making it into cloth-sifted powder, one should put it inside a casket.
This indeed is the supreme and excellent <s>gomedaka-rasāyana</s>.
It should be applied in all diseases, with the vehicle appropriate to each particular disease.

children.text: karoti dīpanaṃ tīvraṃ sarvārhaṃ ca priyaṃkaram
children.translated_text: It produces intense digestive stimulation, is suitable for all, and is pleasing.
It gives supreme nourishment and strength like the terrible strength of <s>Bhīma</s>.
It is supremely aphrodisiac, promotes long life, is good for the eyes, and removes diseases of the mouth.
<s>Vaidūrya</s> is killed with sulfur together with a paste of magnetic iron.
With eight <s>śāṇas</s> of that ash, take half that amount of killed gold.

children.text: tayoḥ samaṃ tīkṣṇarajo mṛtaṃ rūpyaṃ ca tatsamam
children.translated_text: Add sharp iron powder equal to those two, and killed silver equal to that.

children.text: mṛtaṃ ca vimalaṃ sarvaiḥ samaṃ sarvaṃ vimarditam ||
children.translated_text: Add killed <s>vimala</s>, equal to all of them, and triturate everything together.
Mixed with <s>mocasāra</s>, it should be made into pills and dried.
It should be triturated with <s>śilāja</s>, with a layer half a finger thick.
Placed in the middle of a sand apparatus, it should be cooked gently for half a fortnight.
When it has cooled by itself, one should take it out and, with the essence of <s>kumārī</s> root,
triturate it and dry it; likewise with waters from the root of <s>pīlu</s>,
and similarly with waters from <s>citra</s> root and the essence of <s>kanthārī</s> root.
After drying it with waters produced from old <s>bilva</s>, one should pulverize it.
This is the <s>vaidūryaka-rasāyana</s>, the reviver of the dead.
The <s>rasāyana</s>, in a dose the size of a <s>guñjā</s>, is mixed with ginger juice.
It should be given with waters of <s>citraka</s>, or in unconsciousness from <s>sannipāta</s>.
When lockjaw has occurred, this <s>rasa</s>, in a dose of one <s>valla</s>,
should be carefully rubbed on the feet; then the patient regains movement.
When movement has arisen, cold water should be poured over the head.
When it is sweet and measured at a hundred <s>kumbhas</s>, intense hunger then arises.
Whatever he asks for, whatever is desired, that should be given to him.

children.text: āyuṣye vidyamāne sa sukhī jīvati mānavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If his allotted span of life remains, that human being lives happily.
In diseases produced by the three humors, it should be given in a measure equal to a grain of rice,
mixed with half a <s>pala</s> of sugar; otherwise it kills the patient.
In a disease arising from one humor, and likewise in one born from a combination,
the physician should not give the <s>vaidūryaka-rasāyana</s>.

children.text: dhṛtāni vā tāni samarcitāni sujātiyuktāni ca saṃstutāni
children.translated_text: Gems that are worn or that have been worshipfully honored, endowed with good origin and praised,

children.text: haranti ratnānyakhilaṃ duriṣṭaṃ kurvantyabhīṣṭaṃ satataṃ yatheṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: remove every evil omen and continually produce the desired good exactly as wished.

children.text: harantyalakṣmīṃ satataṃ samastān duṣkarmajātān iha sarvarogān
children.translated_text: They always remove misfortune, all evils born from bad karma here, and every disease.
All <s>rasāyanas</s> produced from gems are life-promoting and beneficial.

children.text: śuddhaṃ lohaṃ kanakarajataṃ bhānulohāśmasāraṃ pūtīlohaṃ dvitayamuditaṃ nāgavaṅgābhidhānam
children.translated_text: Pure metal is gold, silver, copper, iron, and the pair of base metals declared to be lead and tin.

children.text: miśraṃ lohaṃ tritayamuditaṃ pittalaṃ kāṃsyavartaṃ dhātur lohe luha iti mataḥ so'pi kaṣārthavācī ||
children.translated_text: Mixed metal is declared to be threefold: brass, bronze, and bell-metal; the root of 'metal' is held to be <s>luh</s>, and that too conveys the sense of scraping or testing.
Natural, innate, fire-born, mine-born,
and born from the transmutation of <s>rasendra</s>: gold is remembered as fivefold.
That by which the cosmic egg was enclosed, born indeed from the quality of passion,
is called natural gold, difficult even for the gods to obtain.
That gold by whose golden caul <s>Brahmā</s> was enclosed at birth,

children.text: tanmerurūpatāṃ jātaṃ suvarṇaṃ sahajaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: and which came to have the form of <s>Meru</s>, is indeed that innate gold.
The fierce, unbearable, yellow radiance of <s>Śiva</s>, discharged by fire,
became gold; that is indicated as fire-born gold.
