These three kinds of gold are divine and possess sixteen degrees of color.
By merely wearing them, one could make the body free from old age and death.

children.text: tatra tatra girīṇāṃ hi jātaṃ khaniṣu yadbhavet
children.translated_text: Whatever is produced here and there in mines among the mountains,
that, endowed with fourteen degrees of color, removes every disease when eaten.
What is produced by the transmutation of <s>rasendra</s> is called transmutation-born.

children.text: rasāyanaṃ mahāśreṣṭhaṃ pāpaghnaṃ vedhajaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: That transmutation-born gold is a most excellent <s>rasāyana</s> and destroys sin.
Silver, copper, brass, other metals, elephant-metal, tin, mica, pyrites, tin, and mercury:

children.text: yattārajaṃ hi pravadanti rāgataḥ svarṇaṃ kalāvarṇacaturguṇaṃ hi ||
children.translated_text: what they call silver-born gold through coloring has four times the degree of color.

children.text: ghṛṣṭaṃ varṇe ghusṛṇasadṛśaṃ raktavarṇaṃ ca dāhe chede kiṃcit sitam akapilaṃ nirdalaṃ bhūribhāram
children.translated_text: Good gold, when rubbed, is like saffron in color; when heated it is red, when cut somewhat white, not tawny, without flakes, and very heavy.

children.text: snigdhaṃ svarṇaṃ ravivirahitaṃ styānaraktaprabhāḍhyaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ diṣṭam atulitalasaccāruvarṇaṃ ca svarṇam ||
children.translated_text: It is smooth, free from dull solar discoloration, rich in a thick red radiance; such unsurpassed, shining, beautiful gold is regarded as the best.

children.text: rūkṣaṃ vivarṇaṃ malinaṃ kaṭhoraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ca dāhe nikaṣe ca pāṇḍu
children.translated_text: Rough, discolored, dirty, hard gold, black when heated and pale on the touchstone,

children.text: sthūlāṅgakaṃ nirbharakaṃ kaḍāraṃ sphuṭatsuvarṇaṃ daśadhā na śastam ||
children.translated_text: coarse-bodied, overly dense, brownish, or cracked gold is tenfold and is not praised.
From the combination of gold, silver, and the like, a mixed metal arises.

children.text: svarṇakāryaṃ na tena syāttasmāt śuddhir vidhīyate
children.translated_text: Gold-work cannot be done with that; therefore purification is prescribed.

children.text: śodhyaṃ na kevalaṃ svarṇaṃ lohānyanyāni śodhayet ||
children.translated_text: Not only gold should be purified; one should also purify the other metals.
A gold leaf of one <s>karṣa</s> measure, sealed between dishes and joined with sharp mineral,
set in charcoal and blown upon for half a <s>prahara</s>, surely becomes full in color.
For all metals, killing with ash of mercury is the best method.
They call killing with roots middling, and with sulfur and the like inferior.
The killing of one metal with its enemy-metal produces bad qualities.
After making the gold leaves pierceable by thorns, one should smear them.
With ash, mercury, and citron juice they are killed by ten <s>puṭas</s>.

children.text: drute vinikṣipet svarṇe lohamānaṃ mṛtaṃ rasam ||
children.translated_text: Into melted gold one should throw dead mercury in an amount equal to the metal.
Having pulverized it with citron water and combined it with <s>darada</s>,
the gold becomes saffron-colored through twelve <s>puṭas</s>.
With stalk of <s>śleṣmāntaka</s> and with packets of <s>kāñcanāra</s> bark or root, using the <s>puṭas</s> called <s>kukkuṭa</s>,
in a quantity of thirty, it becomes non-revivable and should be used in all formulations.

children.text: sūtena piṣṭikāṃ kṛtvā svarṇaṃ ruddhvā śarāvake
children.translated_text: Having made a paste with mercury, and having enclosed the gold in a small dish,
with a little blue collyrium, it should be burned with small forest-cow-dung cakes.
The ash becomes like saffron and is fit to be used in mercury-based <s>rasāyana</s>.
With the milk of <s>snuhī</s>, asafoetida, cinnabar, realgar, red lead, and sour substances,
when heated ten times in <s>puṭas</s>, gold becomes lifeless.
It is greatly praised for mercury, for <s>rasāyana</s>, and for coloring metals.

children.text: snigdhaṃ medhyaṃ viṣagaraharaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ vṛṣyamagryaṃ yakṣmonmādapraśamanaparaṃ deharogapramāthi
children.translated_text: Gold is smooth, intellect-promoting, removing poison and poison-compounds, nourishing, foremost as an aphrodisiac, intent on pacifying consumption and insanity, and a crusher of bodily diseases.

children.text: medhābuddhismṛtisukhakaraṃ sarvadoṣāmayaghnaṃ rucyaṃ dīpi praśamitajaraṃ svādupākaṃ suvarṇam ||
children.translated_text: It gives intelligence, understanding, memory, and happiness; destroys all disorders and diseases; is appetizing, kindling, calming to old age, and sweet in post-digestive effect.

children.text: etadbhasma suvarṇajaṃ kaṭughṛtopetaṃ dviguñjonmitaṃ līḍhaṃ hanti nṛṇāṃ kṣayāgnisadanaṃ śvāsaṃ sakāsārucim
children.translated_text: This ash born of gold, mixed with pungent substance and ghee, in a two-<s>guñjā</s> measure and licked, destroys in people wasting, failure of digestive fire, dyspnea, cough, and loss of appetite.

children.text: ojodhātuvivardhanaṃ balakaraṃ pāṇḍvāmayadhvaṃsanaṃ vṛṣyaṃ sarvaviṣāpahaṃ garaharaṃ duṣṭagrahaṇyādinut ||
children.translated_text: It increases <s>ojas</s> and the bodily tissues, gives strength, destroys anemia, is aphrodisiac, removes every poison, removes compounded poison, and dispels disorders such as bad assimilation.
It destroys every disease without remainder and removes fear of spirits and ghosts.
It restrains future diseases and removes fear of the three kinds of poison.
Here, except for the fruit of <s>bilva</s>, everything else is praised.
For one who has used gold for ten years, moving and eating as he pleases,
no disease afflicts him for as long as his life lasts; there is no doubt.

children.text: sahajaṃ khanisaṃjātaṃ kṛtrimaṃ ca tridhā matam
children.translated_text: Silver is considered threefold: natural, mine-born, and artificial.
Indeed, each earlier kind of silver is progressively better by its own qualities.
Silver produced from mountains such as <s>Kailāsa</s> is natural.
When touched by that, it destroys great diseases in embodied beings.

children.text: himācalādrikūṭeṣu yad rūpyaṃ jāyate hi tat
children.translated_text: The silver that is produced on the peaks of <s>Himācala</s>

children.text: khanijaṃ kathyate tajjñaiḥ paramaṃ hi rasāyanam ||
children.translated_text: is called mine-born by those who know; it is an excellent <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative).
Tin that, when placed at the sandals of <s>Śrīrāma</s>, has become silver
is called foot-silver; it is artificial and removes all diseases.

children.text: ghanaṃ snigdhaṃ mṛdu svacchaṃ dāhe chede sitaṃ guru
children.translated_text: Dense, unctuous, soft, clear, white when burned and cut, heavy,
conch-like, smooth, and without fissures: such silver is auspicious.

children.text: dāhe raktaṃ ca pītaṃ ca kṛṣṇaṃ rūkṣaṃ sphuṭaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: Silver that on burning is red or yellow, black, dry, cracked, light,

children.text: sthūlāṅgaṃ karkaśāṅgaṃ ca rajataṃ tyājyam aṣṭadhā ||
children.translated_text: with a coarse body and a harsh body, should be rejected in these eight ways.
In a potsherd one should make a surrounding rim with ash and powder.
Having placed silver there together with an equal amount of lead,
one should blow on it again and again until the produced lead is exhausted.
Then the silver, clear and purified, should be used in mercury and other preparations.
One should prepare a silver <s>piṣṭī</s> (amalgam or triturated paste) with the juices of <s>lakuca</s> and mercury.

children.text: ūrdhvādho gandhakaṃ dattvā mūṣāgarbhe nirudhya ca ||
children.translated_text: After placing sulfur above and below, and sealing it inside a crucible,
one should heat it in a sand apparatus for one day with a strong fire.

children.text: svāṅgaśītāṃ ca tāṃ piṣṭīṃ sāmlatālena marditām ||
children.translated_text: When that <s>piṣṭī</s> has cooled of itself, it should be triturated with acidic <s>tāla</s>.
One should give it twelve <s>puṭas</s> (closed heating cycles); the silver becomes ash.
When it is triturated with powdered <s>mākṣika</s> and the sour juice of citron, and gently heated by <s>puṭa</s>,
after thirty repetitions that silver indeed becomes ash.

children.text: rāgaḥ syāt sarvalohānāṃ puṭādhikye na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: When the <s>puṭas</s> are increased, there will be coloration of all metals; there is no doubt.
Red substances also color them, accomplishing the purposes of both body and metals.

children.text: rūpyaṃ vipākamadhuraṃ tuvarāmlasāraṃ śītaṃ saraṃ paramalekhanakaṃ ca rucyam
children.translated_text: Silver is sweet in post-digestive effect, astringent and sour in essence, cooling, mobile, an excellent scraper, and agreeable.

children.text: snigdhaṃ ca vātakaphajijjaṭharāgnidīpi balyapradaṃ sthiravayaskaraṇaṃ ca vṛṣyam ||
children.translated_text: It is unctuous, conquers wind and phlegm, kindles the gastric fire, gives strength, stabilizes age, and is aphrodisiac.

children.text: bhasmībhūtaṃ rajatamamalaṃ tatsamau vyomabhānū sarvaistulyaṃ trikaṭukalitaṃ sāraghājyena yuktam
children.translated_text: Pure silver reduced to ash, together with equal parts of mica and copper, mixed with <s>trikaṭu</s> and joined with <s>sāraga</s> ghee,

children.text: līḍhaṃ prātaḥ kṣapayatitarāṃ yakṣmapāṇḍūdarārśaḥ kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ nayanajarujaḥ pittarogānaśeṣān ||
children.translated_text: when licked in the morning, completely destroys consumption, anemia, abdominal disease, piles, cough, dyspnea, eye disorders, and all bilious diseases.
Copper is of two kinds, <s>mleccha</s> and <s>Nepālaka</s>; of the two, the <s>Nepāla</s> kind is best.
That produced in a mine other than <s>Nepāla</s> is called <s>mleccha</s>.
It has white, black, and red shades, is emetic, purgative, and hard.
Even when washed, it again becomes black: this is <s>mleccha</s> copper.
Very unctuous, soft, red, able to withstand heavy blows, heavy,
unchanged, and best in qualities: that is called <s>Nepāla</s> copper.
Copper that is pale, black-red, light, accompanied by cracking,
dry-bodied and flaky is not desired in alchemical work.
Nausea, stupor, dizziness, burning, and cutting pains are truly the hard-to-bear defects of copper.
Through purification, freed from its own defects, it becomes nectar-like in taste, potency, and post-digestive effect.
Copper mixed with alkali and acid, melted and supplied with red ochre,
is to be thrown seven times into buffalo buttermilk with cow dung.
It becomes free from the five defects and fit for use in ash preparations.
Thin copper leaves should be smeared with salt.
After being heated and thrown into sour gruel, they are purified after eight repetitions.
Smeared with neem water and salt, and heated eight times,
they are purified, as are arka leaves, by immersion in the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>.
One should make copper leaves resembling palm leaves.

children.text: niṣkvāthya kāñjike yāmaṃ bhasmanā pariśodhya ca
children.translated_text: After boiling them in sour gruel for a <s>yāma</s> and cleansing them with ash,
one should boil them with milk for a <s>yāma</s> and leave them in that same liquid for a day.
For one day they should remain in the muddy pulp of tamarind fruit mixed with salt.
Then they should be enveloped with salt ground in the juice of citron.
After heating, one should immerse them just once in the midst of goat's urine.
One should smear half the quantity of copper with rock salt and the water of cooked lemons.
After heating it, one should throw it into buttermilk mixed with buffalo dung.
That copper, joined with an equal quantity of gold-colored <s>mākṣika</s>,
should be blown once with very strong coals thereafter.
Then, without <s>tāpya</s>, this should be done three times, and afterward one should prepare small disks.
After that, one should keep them for three days in a decoction of <s>trikaṭu</s>.

children.text: utkvāthya bhasmanā mṛjya jalaiḥ prakṣālya sāraghaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having boiled them up, rubbed them with ash, and washed them with excellent waters,
one should smear them three times with sugar mixed with <s>sāraga</s>.
One should heat the copper with forest cow-dung cakes; it becomes equal to gold in qualities.
A copper leaf placed inside a leaf of <s>kumārī</s>
and heated by <s>puṭa</s> becomes pale and free from defects.
Copper purified in this way, devoid of all defects,
becomes fit for <s>rasāyana</s> and supreme for accomplishing effects in the body and metals.

children.text: imāṃ śuddhiṃ vijānāti śivo vā nandikeśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Only <s>Śiva</s> or <s>Nandikeśvara</s> knows this purification,
or the fortunate <s>Somadeva</s>, refuge of all worlds, and no one else.
Copper killed by the strong agent and raised up seven times
becomes free from all defects and similar to nectar.
After smearing copper leaves with mud made from sulfur and stone ground in <s>lakuca</s> juice,
placing them and sealing them inside a pot,
one should cook them properly for the measure of a <s>yāma</s>, draw them out when calcined, and powder them.
Its ash, one <s>valla</s> in measure, wrapped in a betel leaf,
having been eaten, then after it has caused vomiting and purging for two <s>yāmas</s>,
destroys fever in men when it is accompanied by colic and distension.

children.text: viṣaṃ garaṃ ca vegena vāmayatyeva niścitam
children.translated_text: It certainly makes poison and <s>gara</s> poison be vomited out quickly.
Here the wholesome food to be given is cow's buttermilk together with cooked rice.
In excessive purging, excessive vomiting, and excessive burning heat,
one should perform a cooling countermeasure according to what is appropriate in each case.
In excessive vomiting one should resort to roasted pieces of sugarcane, cooled,

children.text: yadvā bilvabhavaṃ kvāthaṃ sitayā saha pāyayet ||
children.translated_text: or else one should have the patient drink a decoction made from <s>bilva</s>, together with sugar.
Juice of <s>barbūra</s> bark should be drunk in purging, together with buttermilk.
With mercury equal to the copper, and strong sulfur equal to that,
with <s>tāla</s> half that amount, and with <s>śilā</s> half of that,
one should make a smooth <s>kajjalī</s>, resembling separated collyrium.
Inside the belly of the womb-apparatus described in the chapter on apparatus,
one should place that <s>kajjalī</s> and copper leaves alternately.
One should cook it for the duration of a <s>yāma</s>; when it has cooled by itself, one should pulverize it.

children.text: tāmraṃ tiktakaṣāyakaṃ ca madhuraṃ pāke ca vīryoṣṇakaṃ sāmlaṃ pittakaphāpahaṃ jaṭhararukkuṣṭhāmajūrttyantakṛt
children.translated_text: Copper is bitter and astringent, also sweet, pungent in digestion, hot in potency, slightly sour, removing pitta and kapha, and ending abdominal pain, skin disease, <s>āma</s>, and <s>jūrtti</s>.

children.text: ūrdhvādhaḥ pariśodhanaṃ viṣayakṛtsthaulyāpahaṃ kṣutkaraṃ durnāmakṣayapāṇḍurogaśamanaṃ netryaṃ paraṃ lekhanam ||
children.translated_text: It purifies upward and downward, counteracts poison, liver disease, and obesity, stimulates appetite, pacifies piles, wasting, and anemia, benefits the eyes, and is supremely scraping.

children.text: tattadrogaharānupānasahitaṃ tāmraṃ dvivallonmitaṃ saṃlīḍhaṃ pariṇāmaśūlamudaraṃ śūlaṃ ca pāṇḍuṃ jvaram
children.translated_text: Copper measuring two <s>vallas</s>, licked up with vehicles that remove the corresponding diseases, removes post-digestive colic, abdominal disease, colic, anemia, and fever,

children.text: gulmaplīhayakṛtkṣayāgnisadanaṃ mehaṃ ca mūlāmayaṃ duṣṭāṃ ca grahaṇīṃ hared dhruvamidaṃ tatsomanāthābhidham ||
children.translated_text: abdominal tumors, diseases of the spleen and liver, wasting, weak digestion, urinary disease, piles, and a bad <s>grahaṇī</s>; this, called <s>Somanātha</s>, surely removes them.
There is no other preparation equal to this copper, sweet and free from defects.
There is no other that destroys all defects without remainder, is aphrodisiac, and is suitable for healthy people.
With sulfur in the measure of one <s>pala</s>, and with those substances in amounts equal to the powder,
namely the best <s>viṣatindu</s>, <s>agni</s>, <s>śamyāka</s>, <s>vatsanābha</s>, and salts,
with <s>kalihārī</s>, <s>śilā</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>tāla</s>, <s>pūga</s>, and <s>karañja</s>,
one should make a powder and liquefy it thoroughly with lemon juice.

children.text: tatsarvaṃ khalvake bhāṇḍe vinikṣipya tataḥ param
children.translated_text: One should put all that into a mortar-vessel, and after that,
copper leaves of one <s>pala</s>, pierced with artificial points,
and smeared with mercury to a quarter part, should be buried in that paste.

children.text: etat sarvaguṇāḍhyatāprabhavitaṃ śrīsomadevoditaṃ guñjāyugmamitaṃ kaṇājyasahitaṃ saṃsevitaṃ hanti vai
children.translated_text: This, brought forth as endowed with every quality and taught by the venerable <s>Somadeva</s>, when taken in a dose of two <s>guñjās</s> with black pepper and ghee, indeed destroys

abdominal tumors, disorders of the spleen and liver, constipation, abdominal disease, colic, weak digestion, diseases, disorders of vāta and phlegm, wasting, anemia, and <s>jūrtti</s> disease when eaten.
A wholesome regimen appropriate to the disease should be given; sour taste should be avoided.
By the person by whom this has been made habitual, death has been conquered.

children.text: muṇḍaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca kāntaṃ ca triḥprakāramayaḥ smṛtam
children.translated_text: <s>Muṇḍa</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>kānta</s>: iron is remembered as threefold.

children.text: mṛdu kuṇṭhaṃ kaḍāraṃ ca trividhaṃ muṇḍamucyate ||
children.translated_text: Soft, dull, and <s>kaḍāra</s>: <s>muṇḍa</s> is said to be threefold.
That which melts quickly, does not burst, is smooth, soft, and good,
and which, when struck, spreads with difficulty, is remembered as the middling <s>muṇḍa</s>.
That <s>muṇḍa</s> which breaks when bent and is black is <s>kaḍāraka</s>.
The best <s>muṇḍa</s>, very soft, removes kapha- and vāta-colic, piles, <s>āma</s>, urinary disease, jaundice, and anemia;

children.text: gulmāmavātajaṭharārttiharaṃ pradīpi śophāpahaṃ rudhirakṛt khalu koṣṭhaśodhi ||
children.translated_text: it removes abdominal tumors, <s>āmavāta</s>, and abdominal pain, stimulates digestion, removes swelling, produces blood, and cleanses the bowel.

children.text: kharaṃ sāraṃ ca honnālaṃ tārāpaṭṭaṃ ca bhājaram
children.translated_text: <s>Khara</s>, <s>sāra</s>, <s>honnāla</s>, <s>tārāpaṭṭa</s>, and <s>bhājara</s>,
and that named <s>kālaloha</s>: <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is said to be sixfold.
Rough, free from <s>pogara</s>, and in fracture having the true lustre of mercury,
that which bends yet is brittle is declared to be <s>kharaloha</s>.
That whose edge breaks rapidly is called <s>sāraloha</s>.
<s>Sāra</s> is said to be pale, earthy, and resembling <s>yogara</s>.
With a black-and-pale body, resembling the seed of <s>cañcu</s>, broad, and like <s>yogara</s>,
and very rough when cut, it is called <s>honnāla</s>.
Covered with <s>yogaras</s> like diamonds, with fine and dense lines,

children.text: nicitaṃ śyāmalāṅgaṃ ca bhājaraṃ tat prakīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: and dark in body, that is proclaimed to be <s>bhājara</s>.
Blue-black in appearance, dense, smooth, heavy, and shining,
with an edge that is not broken even by blows from iron, it is considered <s>kālāyasa</s>.
Everything after <s>kharaloha</s> is superior, each by a hundredfold.

children.text: rūkṣaṃ syāt kharalohakaṃ sumadhuraṃ pāke ca vīrye himaṃ tiktoṣṇaṃ kaphapittakuṣṭhajaṭharaplīhāmapāṇḍvartinut
children.translated_text: <s>Kharaloha</s> is dry, very sweet in digestion and cold in potency, bitter and hot, removing kapha, pitta, skin disease, abdominal disease, spleen disease, <s>āma</s>, anemia, and pain;

children.text: sadyaḥ śūlayakṛdgadakṣayajarāmehāmavātāpahaṃ dīptaṃ cātirasāyanaṃ balakaraṃ durnāmamedo'paham ||
children.translated_text: it quickly removes colic, liver disease, wasting, old age, urinary disease, and <s>āmavāta</s>; it is radiant, an excellent <s>rasāyana</s>, strength-giving, and removes piles and fat.
<s>Kāntaloha</s> is said to be fourfold: <s>romaka</s>, <s>bhrāmaka</s>,

children.text: cumbakaṃ drāvakaṃ ceti teṣu śreṣṭhaṃ paraṃ param ||
children.translated_text: <s>cumbaka</s>, and <s>drāvaka</s>; among them each successive one is superior to the preceding.
Because, from magnetic stones that are being excavated,

children.text: satejāṃsi hi romāṇi kāntaṃ tadromakaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: lustrous hair-like filaments emerge, that magnetic iron is considered <s>romaka</s>.
In some places on excellent mountains the <s>bhrāmaka</s> stone is easily found.
When iron is thrown at its mouth, it surely turns like a wheel.
On Mount <s>Vindhya</s>, magnet stones attract an iron nail,
and quickly draw it in, just as a woman draws the mind of young men.
That which, when touched, melts iron, gold, and the rest completely,
is obtained only with great difficulty on Mount <s>Tuṣāradhara</s>.

children.text: pātre yasya prasarati jale tailabindurna lipto hiṅgurgandhaṃ visṛjati nijaṃ tiktatāṃ nimbakalkaḥ
children.translated_text: In a vessel of which an oil-drop spreads out on water and is not smeared, asafoetida gives up its own smell and neem paste its bitterness;

children.text: pācyaṃ dugdhaṃ bhavati śikharākārakaṃ naiti bhūmau kāntaṃ lohaṃ tadidamuditaṃ lakṣaṇoktaṃ na cānyat ||
children.translated_text: milk cooked in it takes on a peaked form and does not go down to the ground. This metal is declared to be <s>kānta</s> by the stated marks, and no other.

children.text: kāntāyo 'tirasāyanottarataraṃ svasthe cirāyuḥpradaṃ snigdhaṃ mehaharaṃ tridoṣaśamanaṃ śūlāmamūlāpaham
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s> iron is better than the best among <s>rasāyana</s>s, gives long life to the healthy, is unctuous, removes urinary disorders, pacifies the three <s>doṣa</s>s, and removes colic, undigested matter, and piles.

children.text: gulmaplīhayakṛtkṣayāmayaharaṃ pāṇḍūdaravyādhinut tiktoṣṇaṃ himavīryakaṃ kimaparaṃ yogena sarvārtinut ||
children.translated_text: It removes abdominal tumors, spleen and liver disease, wasting disease, anemia, and abdominal disorders; it is bitter, hot, and cooling in potency. What more need be said? Used in a proper compound, it removes every affliction.
Every metal is successively a hundred-thousand times better than the preceding one;
among them <s>kānta</s> is ten-millionfold in quality, and that too is thus superior in qualities.
All iron, beginning with <s>muṇḍa</s>, smeared with hare's blood
and thoroughly heated three times, gives up all its defects.
When heated with sea salt and then certainly quenched
in a decoction of <s>triphala</s>, iron gives up its mountain-born defects.
A decoction of tamarind fruit and leaves and the like drives out the defect;
or else, together with the three fruits, it may be boiled for a short time in cow's urine.
Iron that has been filed, sprinkled with ghee, and placed in a potsherd pan should be cooked,

children.text: cālayan lohadaṇḍena yāvat kṣiptaṃ tṛṇaṃ dahet ||
children.translated_text: stirring it with an iron rod until a blade of grass thrown in is burnt.
Grinding and grinding it, one should cook it in this way five times; thereafter,
with juices of <s>dhātrī</s> leaves or with waters boiled with <s>triphala</s>,
one should calcine the iron in <s>puṭa</s>s four times; it will indeed float on water.
Leaves of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron, made without layers, should be heated in a strong fire;
after heating them, one should at once throw them into water inside a stone mortar,
and pound them with extremely forceful blows by means of a large iron pestle.
From within that, the coarse pieces should be enclosed between two crucibles;

children.text: dhmātvā siktvā jalaiḥ samyak pūrvavat kaṇḍayet khalu ||
children.translated_text: after heating them and properly sprinkling them with water, one should pound them as before.
That powder should be calcined twenty times with jaggery and sulfur;
at each <s>puṭa</s>, grinding must be done more and more firmly.
Iron reduced to ash in this way should be applied in the respective diseases.
Now the previously described <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron, with the leaf-water of <s>bhallaka</s> and <s>vāsā</s>,
should be carefully calcined thirty times;
the ash becomes red, taking on the appearance of prepared vermilion.
Or else the dust produced from leaves of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron should be ground with <s>triphala</s> water;
having added a little cooked rice and made small disks,
one should dry them with great care and cook them with five <s>puṭa</s>s;
that red-colored ash should be used as appropriate.
With <s>matsyākṣī</s>, sulfur, and <s>vāhlīka</s>, ground in the juice of <s>lakuca</s>,
one should smear all the iron, covering it with a paste of <s>matsyākṣī</s>;
then one should blow it very strongly with two bellows until the three-pronged discharge appears,
and afterward take it out and cast it into a decoction made of <s>triphala</s> and cow's urine.
Having taken it from that, beaten it, and taken the dead iron,
one should again heat it as before and kill all the iron.
Then, after pounding it together with sulfur, jaggery, and <s>triphala</s>,
one should calcine it twenty times; it certainly becomes non-revivable.
Iron powder with an equal quantity of sulfur, kneaded with the water of <s>kumārī</s>,
is heaped up and kept in the shade for some time; the iron is indeed killed.

children.text: etatsyādapunarbhavaṃ hi bhasitaṃ lohasya divyāmṛtaṃ samyak siddharasāyanaṃ trikaṭukīvellājyamadhvanvitam
children.translated_text: This is the non-revivable ash of iron, a divine nectar, a properly perfected <s>rasāyana</s>, combined with <s>trikaṭukī</s>, <s>vellā</s>, ghee, and honey.

children.text: hanyānniṣkamitaṃ jarāṃ ca maraṇaṃ vyādhīṃśca satputradaṃ diṣṭaṃ śrīgiriśena kālayavanodbhūtyai purā tatpituḥ ||
children.translated_text: Taken in a <s>niṣka</s> measure, it destroys old age, death, and diseases, and gives a good son; long ago <s>Śrīgiriśa</s> prescribed it to the father of <s>Kālayavana</s> for the birth of <s>Kālayavana</s>.
For those who take this regularly, heaps of diseases do not arise,
and a prosperous son is born, endowed with intelligence, firmness, and strength.
This ash should be prepared from black iron together with <s>kānta</s> iron;
ash made from other iron does not possess such qualities.
Or that iron, ground with the milk of <s>matsyākṣī</s>, sulfur, and stone,
when calcined twenty times, becomes non-revivable ash.
One should cook that ash, eight <s>pala</s>s in quantity, with cow's urine eight times its measure,
in an iron vessel, stirring it with an iron ladle.
This iron prepared in such a manner, in a dose measured as two <s>valla</s>s,
destroys all diseases produced from the respective <s>doṣa</s>s:

children.text: kṣayaṃ pāṇḍugadaṃ gulmaṃ śūlaṃ mūlāmayaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: wasting disease, anemia, abdominal tumor, colic, and piles,

children.text: mehaṃ medo'gnimāndyaṃ ca yakṛtplīhaṃ ca kāmalām ||
children.translated_text: urinary disease, obesity, weak digestion, liver and spleen disorders, and jaundice,

children.text: śvāsaṃ kāsaṃ ca kuṣṭhaṃ ca jvaraṃ śūlānvitaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: dyspnea, cough, skin disease, and fever accompanied by pain as well.

children.text: kāntaṃ tulyābhrasattvaṃ caraṇaparimitaṃ hema tattulyamarkaṃ vaikrāntaṃ tāpyarūpyaṃ krimiripukaṭukais tulyabhāgaiḥ sametam
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s> iron, an equal quantity of mica essence, gold measured as a quarter, copper equal to that, <s>vaikrānta</s>, <s>tāpya</s>, and silver, combined in equal parts with <s>krimiripu</s> and pungent substances,

children.text: līḍhaṃ devadrutailaiḥ pravitarati nṛṇāṃ dehasiddhiṃ samṛddhāṃ pathyaṃ pūrvoktavat taddharati ca sakalaṃ rogapūgaṃ javena ||
children.translated_text: when licked with oils of <s>devadru</s>, grants men abundant perfection of the body; the regimen is as stated before, and it swiftly removes the whole mass of diseases.
This, then, is the lovely <s>kānta-rasāyana</s>, destroyer of all diseases,

children.text: balyaṃ vṛṣyaṃ suputrīyaṃ maṅgalyaṃ dīpanaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: strengthening, aphrodisiac, productive of good sons, auspicious, and supremely kindling digestion.
Half a <s>pala</s> of filed iron, with the liquid of young <s>bilva</s> fruit,
should be ground and ground and cooked quickly; it indeed becomes ash.
Likewise, with the waters of <s>liṅgī</s> fruit and with the juice of <s>dhātrī</s> fruit,
one should kill the iron as before; it becomes richer in qualities.
With the alkalis of <s>punarbhū</s>, <s>sindhu</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>vajriṇī</s>, and tamarind bark,
the <s>bhasma</s> (ash) of all metals, taken in a dose of one <s>śāṇa</s>, is to be used.
A man should drink every month a decoction joined with <s>triphala</s>,
for the purification from iron dross; otherwise a urinary stone arises.
Unpurified iron is held to cause vomiting like poison.

children.text: nandinā tu viśuddhyarthaṃ lohaṃ proktaṃ sudhāsamam ||
children.translated_text: But for purification, iron has been taught by <s>Nandin</s> to be equal to nectar.

children.text: rātrau kāntaśarāvake sthitavarāmitrājalaiḥ svādubhiḥ prātarmuṣṭimitaṃ khalu pratidinaṃ ṣaṇmāsam āsevitam
children.translated_text: At night, in a small <s>kānta</s> saucer, <s>varā</s> kept with sweet waters of <s>mitrā</s>, taken each morning in a fist-sized amount every day for six months,

children.text: hanyātpittakaphāmayān bahuvidhānkuṣṭhapramehāṃstathā pāṇḍuṃ yakṣmagadaṃ ca kāmalagadaṃ mūlāmayaṃ vātajān ||
children.translated_text: destroys many diseases of bile and phlegm, as well as skin diseases, urinary disorders, anemia, consumption, jaundice, piles, and diseases born of wind.
Unpurified iron, reverting again and displaying those qualities, then in a short time would produce
undigested matter, weak digestive fire, loss of taste, abdominal tumor, swelling, diarrhea, lassitude, and obstruction in the chest.
Tin is said to be of two kinds: <s>khuraka</s> and <s>miśraka</s>.

children.text: khuraṃ tatra guṇaiḥ śreṣṭhaṃ miśrakaṃ na hitaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: Of these, <s>khura</s> is best in qualities; <s>miśraka</s> is considered unsuitable.

children.text: dhavalaṃ ca mṛdu snigdhaṃ drutadrāvaṃ sagauravam
children.translated_text: White, soft, unctuous, quickly melting, and heavy,
without sound, is <s>khura</s> tin; <s>miśraka</s> is dark and pale mixed together.
Tin is bitter, hot, dry, and slightly aggravates wind.
It destroys diseases of fat and phlegm, kills worms, and removes urinary disorders.
After it has been melted, when thrown into the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> mixed with <s>niśā</s>,
<s>khura</s> tin is purified after three repetitions; there is no doubt.
With <s>varṣābhū</s>, <s>viṣa</s>, and <s>sindhu</s> ground in sour buttermilk,
tin placed inside a bitter bottle-gourd is purified by the second method.
Then, after smearing leaves of tin with orpiment and the milk of <s>arka</s>,
one should give them light <s>puṭas</s> (heatings) with the alkalis of <s>bodhiciñcā</s> bark.
After grinding it, one should make the ash; it is praised for mercurial and similar preparations.

children.text: pradrāvya kharpare vaṅgaṃ ṣoḍaśāṃśaṃ rasaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Having melted the tin in an earthen basin, one should add mercury in a sixteenth part.
Adding <s>ālaka</s> little by little, using the wood of <s>Bhāradvāja</s>,
after grinding it one should make the ash; it is declared for mercurial and similar preparations.
Equal to the tin ash should be <s>kānta</s>, and mica ash equal to that.
One should triturate them with the water of <s>kanyakā</s> and also with neem-leaf juice.
Then, adding an equal portion of <s>bhūpālāvarta</s> ash,
one should grind it thoroughly with cow urine and waters of <s>śilādhātu</s>.
Then, after triturating it with guggulu water for eight days,
one should dry it, powder it finely, and combine it in equal proportion.
With roasted exudates of <s>barbūra</s> and powders of <s>vākucī</s> seed,
then one should place it inside a casket, after filtering it through cloth.
One should administer it together with the essence of turmeric ground in cow buttermilk.
Equal to four <s>vallakas</s>, it is a pleasing tin <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenating preparation).
By it, certainly, the twenty varieties of urinary disease perish.
Rice, mung-bean soup, fresh butter, and sesame oil,
<s>paṭola</s>, bitter <s>tuṇḍīra</s>, and buttermilk are commended as wholesome.
That which melts quickly, is very heavy, black and bright when cut,
has a foul smell and is black on the outside is pure lead; anything otherwise is not.
Lead is very hot, unctuous, bitter, and removes wind.
It destroys urinary disorders and fluid defects, kindles digestion, and lessens <s>āmavāta</s>.
In a decoction of <s>sinduvāra</s> roots one should place turmeric powder.
Molten lead should be thrown three times into the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>.
Lead purified in this way does not cause fainting, eruptions, and the like.
In a cross-shaped hearth one should place a pot with its mouth turned sideways.

children.text: taṃ ca vaktraṃ vinā sarvaṃ gopayedyatnato mṛdā
children.translated_text: With care one should cover all of it with clay, except for that mouth.
This is called the <s>bhrāṣṭra-yantra</s>, the best method for killing lead.
In that apparatus called the <s>bhrāṣṭra-yantra</s>, one should place lead.
One should put in twenty <s>palas</s> of lead and set a strong fire below.

children.text: drute nāge kṣipetsūtaṃ śuddhaṃ karṣamitaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: When the lead is melted, one should add good purified mercury measuring one <s>karṣa</s>.

children.text: vighaṭṭya nikṣipet kṣāramekaikaṃ hi palaṃ palam ||
children.translated_text: After stirring it, one should add alkali, each one <s>pala</s> by one <s>pala</s>.
Of the tree called <s>arjuna</s>, and also of <s>mahārājagiri</s>,

children.text: dāḍimasya mayūrasya kṣiptvā kṣāraṃ pṛthak pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: of pomegranate and of <s>mayūra</s>, one should add the alkalis separately.
Thus for twenty nights one should cook it with a fierce fire,

children.text: vighaṭṭayan dṛḍhaṃ dorbhyāṃ darvyā cātha prayatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: stirring it firmly with both arms and then carefully with a ladle.
That ash becomes red, and also of a dove-gray hue.
The lead, freed from defects, becomes a <s>rasāyana</s>.
Lead that has been killed and raised up becomes perfected after ten repetitions.
That dead lead, free from all defects, is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
Thus the ash produced from lead should be combined with half as much <s>tāpya</s> ash.

children.text: pādaṃ pādaṃ kṣipedbhasma śulbasya rajatasya ca ||
children.translated_text: One should add a quarter and a quarter of the ashes of copper and of silver,
and also of <s>kānta</s> and mica essence, and of crystal, each separately.
Having powdered everything together, one should heat it by <s>puṭa</s> with <s>triphala</s> water.
With thirty <s>vanagiriṇḍas</s>, one should powder it thirty times.
One should combine it with equal parts of the powders of <s>vyoṣa</s> and <s>vellaka</s>.
Licked with honey and ghee in a dose of one <s>valla</s>, it destroys
eighty wind-born diseases, especially <s>dhanurvāta</s>.
It destroys all diseases of phlegm without remainder, and all urinary diseases,

children.text: śvāsaṃ kāsaṃ kṣayaṃ pāṇḍuṃ śvayathuṃ śītakaṃ jvaram ||
children.translated_text: dyspnea, cough, wasting, anemia, swelling, coldness, and fever,
as well as <s>grahaṇī</s>, the disorder of undigested matter, and hard-to-conquer weakness of the digestive fire.
and all disorders arising in the rectum, according to the appropriate disease and accompanying drink.
<s>Pittala</s> is of two kinds, called <s>rītikā</s> and <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>.

children.text: saṃtaptā kāñjike kṣiptā tāmrābhā rītikā matā
children.translated_text: When heated and thrown into sour gruel, the copper-colored kind is regarded as <s>rītikā</s>.

children.text: evaṃ prajāyate kṛṣṇā kākatuṇḍīti sā matā ||
children.translated_text: When it becomes black in this same way, it is regarded as <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>.

children.text: gurvī mṛdvī ca pītābhā sārāṅgī tāḍanakṣamā
children.translated_text: Heavy, soft, yellowish, variegated, and able to endure hammering,

children.text: susnigdhā masṛṇāṅgī ca rītikā tādṛśī śubhā ||
children.translated_text: very unctuous and smooth-bodied: such <s>rītikā</s> is good.
Pale, rough, dry, coarse, and unable to withstand rubbing,
foul-smelling and light: such <s>rīti</s> is not desired in mercury and related preparations.
<s>Rīti</s> is bitter in taste, dry, worm-killing, and removes bloody bilious disorders;
when used in formulations it removes worms and skin disease, and, though hot in potency, it is cooling.
<s>Kākatuṇḍī</s>, devoid of unctuousness, bitter and hot, removes phlegm and bile;
it is proclaimed to remove diseases of the liver and spleen, and to be cooling in potency.
When heated and thrown into the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> mixed with black powder,
<s>rīti</s> certainly attains purification after five repetitions.
Covered with lemon juice, <s>śilā</s>, and sulfur, and heated by <s>puṭa</s> eight times,
<s>rīti</s> becomes ash; thereafter it is to be applied as appropriate.
Powder of gold-colored <s>rītikā</s>, eaten and then voided
by a black goat that is young and intoxicated,

children.text: talliptaṃ kharpare dagdhaṃ drutiṃ muñcati śobhanām
children.translated_text: when smeared on a potsherd and burnt, releases a fine molten essence.
Its appearance is like gold shining with a fourteenfold bright color.
It is said to effect the body and metals, and is suited to mercury and <s>rasāyana</s>.
Calcined <s>ārakūṭa</s>, <s>kānta</s>, and killed essence of mica,
these three in equal parts, combined with equal <s>vyoṣa</s> and <s>jantughna</s>,
and joined with <s>brahmabīja</s>, <s>ajamodā</s>, <s>agni</s>, <s>bhallātaka</s>, and sesame,
when taken in the measure of a <s>niṣka</s>, is vermicidal and destroys skin disease;
it especially destroys white leprosy, stimulates appetite, digests, and is beneficial.
With eight parts of copper and two parts of <s>kuṭila</s>,

children.text: vidrutena bhavet kāṃsyaṃ tat saurāṣṭrabhavaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: when these are melted, <s>kāṃsya</s> is produced; that arising from <s>Saurāṣṭra</s> is good.
Sharp-sounding, soft, unctuous, slightly dark and white,

children.text: nirmalaṃ dāharaktaṃ ca ṣoḍhā kāṃsyaṃ praśasyate ||
children.translated_text: clear, and red when heated: <s>kāṃsya</s> having these six qualities is praised.

children.text: yatpītaṃ dahane tāmraṃ kharaṃ rūkṣaṃ ghanāsaham
children.translated_text: That <s>kāṃsya</s> which is yellow, coppery in the fire, rough, dry, and unable to bear blows,
dull-sounding and devoid of luster, should be rejected as having seven faults.

children.text: kāṃsyaṃ laghu ca tiktoṣṇaṃ lekhanaṃ dṛkprasādanam
children.translated_text: <s>Kāṃsya</s> is light, bitter-hot, scraping, and clarifying for the eyes;
it destroys multitudes of worms, removes wind and bile, and is beneficial as a vessel.
Except for ghee alone, everything placed in <s>kāṃsya</s>
and eaten by men gives health and happiness, is wholesome, and makes food suitable.

children.text: taptaṃ kāṃsyaṃ gavāṃ mūtre vāpitaṃ pariśudhyati
children.translated_text: Heated <s>kāṃsya</s>, quenched in cow urine, is purified;
with sulfur and orpiment it is killed, rendered non-revivable by five <s>puṭas</s>.
The metal produced from <s>kāṃsya</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>rīti</s>, iron, and <s>ahi</s>
is that <s>varttaloha</s>; it is also called <s>pañcaloha</s> by knowers of metals.
It is cooling, sour, pungent, dry, and destroys phlegm and bile;

children.text: rucyaṃ tvacyaṃ krimighnaṃ ca netryaṃ malaviśodhanam ||
children.translated_text: it improves taste and skin, kills worms, benefits the eyes, and purifies the stool.
All rice, relishes, and soups prepared in a vessel made of it,

children.text: amlena varjitaṃ cāpi dīpanaṃ pācanaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: provided they are free from acid, are auspicious, appetite-kindling, and digestive.
Molten <s>varttaloha</s> thrown into horse urine is purified;
<s>varttaloha</s>, heated by <s>puṭa</s>, is killed with sulfur and orpiment.
In these various procedures here, it should be employed according to rule,
with materials that are genuine, purified, and prepared by the proper method: namely,
<s>rasas</s>, <s>uparasas</s>, metals, and the like; mercury succeeds, and not otherwise.
Gems, metals, cowries, oyster shells, stone-born substances, hoof, horn, and bone,
and whatever among the <s>mahārasas</s> and the rest has a hard body: when reduced to ash, that is indeed fit for mercury.
For the purpose of liquefying diamonds I shall explain the <s>sattva</s> born from <s>bhūnāga</s>.
That alone is the supreme brilliance of royal mercury and of diamond.
The washed substance produced from <s>bhūnāga</s> should be triturated with juices of <s>bhṛṅga</s>,
and separately for three days with lemon liquids and fresh juices of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>.
Mixed with that melting group, thoroughly triturated, and made into pellets,
it should be sealed in a firm crucible and blown strongly for two <s>daṇḍas</s>.

children.text: svataḥ śītaṃ samāhṛtya paṭṭake viniveśya yat
children.translated_text: When it has cooled by itself, one should collect it and place it on a plate;
the grains, equal to mustard seeds, and even the dust particles, are weighty.
Combined with one-twelfth part <s>arka</s> and blown, one should gather the grains;
with this one should carry out the melting of diamond and the like as desired.
This is called <s>kharasattva</s>, the unsurpassed <s>rasāyana</s>;
from two or three crucibles, one portion of <s>sattva</s> certainly comes forth.
Taking earth-born serpents from soils connected with gold, silver, copper, iron, and <s>kānta</s>,
in a quantity amounting to four <s>prasthas</s>,
one should wash them with turmeric-water and also with cool water.

children.text: upoṣitaṃ mayūraṃ vā śūraṃ vā caraṇāyudham ||
children.translated_text: Then, taking a fasting peacock or a strong rooster,
one should feed them to it in sequence and afterward collect its excrement.

children.text: kṣārāmlaiḥ saha saṃpeṣya viśoṣya ca kharātape ||
children.translated_text: Grinding that with alkalis and acids, and drying it in fierce sunlight,

children.text: tataḥ kharparake kṣiptvā bharjayitvā maṣīṃ caret
children.translated_text: then placing it in a potsherd and roasting it, one should produce a black ash.
The ash, combined with the melting group, should be thoroughly triturated;
after sealing it inside a furnace, one should blow it for two <s>ghaṭikās</s>.
From the cooled crucible one should remove the ingot and grind it;
washing it, one should at once carefully gather the grains.
Having blown it in the manner of gold, one should make it into grains and employ it.

children.text: bhūnāgodbhavasattvam uttamatamaṃ śrīsomadevoditaṃ dattaṃ pādamitaṃ dviśāṇakanake kurvīta tenormikām
children.translated_text: One should take the very best essence produced from <s>bhūnāga</s>, as taught by the venerable <s>Somadeva</s>, a quarter measure, with gold of two <s>śāṇas</s>, and make from it a ring.

children.text: taddhautāmbuvilepanaṃ sthiracarodbhūtaṃ viṣaṃ netraruk śūlaṃ mūlagadaṃ ca karṇajarujo hanyāt prasūtigraham ||
children.translated_text: Water in which that has been washed, and smearing with it, destroys poison arising from stationary and moving beings, eye pain, colic, piles, ear disorders, and the afflicting <s>graha</s> of childbirth.
And <s>aṅkola</s> oil is described for the making of mercury ash and the like
by the illustrious sons of <s>Deva</s>, great ministers of meritorious fame.
One should make a very dense paste from old <s>aṅkola</s> seeds
and place an <s>āḍhaka</s> measure in a jar, sealing it up.
Into the hole in the bottom of the jar one should insert an iron rod.
In a well-made pit, low down and one and a half cubits across,

children.text: tatra prādeśike gartte sīsapātraṃ nidhāya ca
children.translated_text: and in that pit, of a span's measure, one should place a lead vessel.

children.text: paṭaṃ ca paribaddhvā tu sandhibandhaṃ samācaret ||
children.translated_text: Then one should tie on a cloth and seal the joints.

children.text: laddibhiḥ pūrayed gartaṃ kaṇṭhāvadhi tataḥ param
children.translated_text: After that, one should fill the pit with fuel cakes up to the neck.
After six months one should take out the oil that is in the lead vessel.

children.text: tena tailena saṃklinnāḥ pāṣāṇā ye bhuvartikāḥ
children.translated_text: Stones, the <s>bhuvartikas</s>, soaked with that oil

children.text: kūpe prakṣālitāḥ kṣiptā jvalanti niśi te ciram ||
children.translated_text: and then washed and thrown into a well, burn for a long time at night.
Likewise, a seed smeared with it, as stated, certainly sprouts.
Mercury is bound and killed by this oil; this is certain.
Split chickpeas kept in that oil for just a month
when eaten in a quarter portion, purge sixty times.

children.text: takraṃ bhaktaṃ tataḥ pathyaṃ dātavyaṃ rekaśāntaye
children.translated_text: Then buttermilk and rice, as wholesome diet, should be given to stop the purging.
At the end of a fortnight one should purge as before with half a split pulse.

children.text: tato dālī tripādena cūrṇārdhena tataḥ param
children.translated_text: Then with three quarters of a split pulse, and after that with half a portion of powder,

children.text: pakṣe pakṣe virekeṇa sarvaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ vinaśyati ||
children.translated_text: by purging fortnight after fortnight, every <s>kuṣṭha</s> disease is destroyed.
All diseases curable by purgation are destroyed; there is no doubt.
All diseases curable by purgation are destroyed, and especially white <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
Purified mercury, the measure of a <s>guñjā</s>, with only a drop of the oil,
ground on a leaf of <s>ahilatā</s> and eaten together with the leaf,
at that very moment produces a blazing, forceful digestive fire.
It also makes the man who uses it an excessive eater, like a wolf.
This <s>aṅkola</s> oil indeed brings about effects in the body and in metals.
By smearing with this oil, white <s>kuṣṭha</s> is destroyed.
This <s>aṅkola</s> oil is declared to be a great essence.
It becomes thick like ghee; all that has been described here.
<s>Aṅkola</s> seeds without their skins and slightly crushed
should be sealed in a <s>vidyādhara</s> apparatus and cooked slowly for half a <s>daṇḍa</s>.
The oil that has gone into the upper pot should be placed on a <s>nāgavallī</s> leaf.
In that, one should grind mercury the measure of a <s>guñjā</s> and swallow it together with the leaf.

children.text: kuryād dīpanam uddhataṃ gurutaradravyādisaṃcūrṇanaṃ hanyādaṣṭavidhaṃ ca gulmam aruciṃ plīhāmayaṃ svāmayam
children.translated_text: It produces powerful kindling of digestion and the pulverizing of very heavy substances and the like; it destroys the eight kinds of <s>gulma</s>, loss of appetite, spleen disease, and one's own disorder,

children.text: śvitrādyaṃ sakalaṃ ca kuṣṭhamacirātpāṇḍvāmayaṃ ca jvaraṃ śūlaṃ mūlagadaṃ tathā śvayathukaṃ śvāsaṃ ca kāsaṃ nṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: as well as all <s>kuṣṭha</s> beginning with <s>śvitra</s>, quickly, and also anemia, fever, colic, piles, swelling, dyspnea, and cough in men.
<s>Aṅkola</s> seeds freed of hard matter should be made small with hot water
and placed in a sack; thereafter they should be made skinless.
Then, in alkali situated in a vessel, one should indeed pour in water,
and add crushed roots of <s>tilaparṇī</s> there in the proper measure.
After it has remained there for two nights, one should transfer it to another vessel.
When it is dry, one should put the oil that has come out into a lead casket.
Split chickpeas should remain there for three months.
Then, on the first occasion, one should give just a quarter measure to a <s>kuṣṭha</s> patient.
By it he is quickly purged thirty times; after that,
wholesome food with rice should be given, excluding greens.
Thus, when he has certainly been purged constantly every ten days,
he is freed from all <s>kuṣṭha</s> diseases in six or seven rounds.
It is declared equal in virtues to the oil previously described.
Having crushed the roots of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s> with sour gruel,
one should add a crushed paste of <s>aṅkola</s> seeds.
That oil, thick like ghee, is excellent and should be collected according to rule.
Then one should grind the leaves of <s>peṭakārī</s> with <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>.
After that, with sour gruel, one should rub them with that paste.
The powder of <s>aṅkola</s> seeds should be tied in a loosely woven cloth.
One should hang it in strong sunlight and place a cup beneath it.
The oil that falls there is to be taken; it destroys <s>śvitra</s>.
The powder arising from <s>aṅkola</s> seeds, after being well rubbed with sour gruel,
should be left for one night and then made into a lump.
Then one should steam it in a <s>kanduka</s> apparatus for two <s>ghaṭikās</s>.

children.text: tāṃ ca piṇḍīṃ dṛḍhe vastre baddhvā niṣpīḍya kāṣṭhataḥ
children.translated_text: That lump should be tied in a strong cloth and pressed with wood.
One should collect the oil situated in the lower vessel and put it to use.
In this way, by means of the <s>kanduka</s> apparatus, one should obtain all oils.
By the oceans of the path of <s>rasa</s>, almost nothing has been revealed completely.
Now I shall teach the procedure of the king of <s>rasa</s>, in eighteen operations.
The essence of all medicines, beginning with <s>sudhā</s>, is established in mercury.

children.text: amartyā bhavituṃ martyā niṣevadhvaṃ mitho yutam ||
children.translated_text: Mortals, in order to become immortals, should use it in mutual combination.

children.text: āyurvajraṃ vitarati nṛṇām aṅgavarṇaṃ suvarṇaṃ sattvaṃ vyomno madakaribalaṃ tāmram ugrāṃ kṣudhāṃ ca
children.translated_text: It gives men adamantine longevity, golden bodily color, the essence of <s>vyoma</s> (mica), the strength of rutting elephants, copper, and fierce hunger

children.text: māyoḥ śāntiṃ rajatamamalaṃ kāntametatsamastaṃ śrīmān sūtaḥ sakalagadahṛd dehalohe tu siddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>sūta</s>, accomplished in the body and in metals, removes all diseases and brings all this: pacification, stainless silver, and beauty.
At the beginning of a <s>kalpa</s>, when the two <s>Śivas</s>, out of love and from a desire to conquer one another,
had entered into intercourse that shook the three worlds,
Fire was sent by the gods to stop their lovemaking,
because they desired the birth of their son, in order to kill the <s>asura Tāraka</s>.
Fire reached a cave of <s>Himavat</s> in the form of a pigeon,
agitated by his state as a bird and looked upon with a smile of love.
Seeing him, <s>Śambhu</s> was ashamed; at that time he stopped from intercourse,
and with one hand he caught the tejas that had flowed from himself.

children.text: nikṣiptaṃ vadane vahner gaṅgāyām apatacca tat
children.translated_text: Placed in the mouth of Fire, it fell into the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
and the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, being intensely burned, cast it out.
From that, metals of superior qualities arose, equal to nectar;
and what had fallen from <s>Śiva</s>'s hand became <s>pārada</s>.
By it the immortals, the ageless ones, became the foremost of the thirty gods;
and from its respective impurity the metals arose, eight in number.
What fell from the mouth of Fire became <s>rasa</s> indeed;
it was used by the chiefs of serpents, who wished to conquer old age and death.
But what, while being drunk, fell from the mouth of the serpents because of its heaviness,
fell into a well one hundred <s>yojanas</s> deep.

children.text: īṣat pītāntaro rūkṣaḥ sa sūto dehalohakṛt
children.translated_text: Slightly yellow within and rough, that <s>sūta</s> acts upon the body and metals.

children.text: snātāmādyarajasvalāṃ hayagatāṃ prāptāṃ jighṛkṣuśca tāṃ so'pyāgacchati yojanaṃ hi paritaḥ pratyeti kūpaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Wishing to seize a woman who has bathed, is in her first menstruation, and has mounted a horse, it too comes for a <s>yojana</s> around and then returns again to the well.

children.text: tanmārge kṛtagarttake ca bahuśaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate sūtarāṭ so'yaṃ tatra nivāsibhiḥ khalu janairevaṃ samānīyate ||
children.translated_text: On that path, in little pits made there, the king <s>sūta</s> often remains; thus it is brought together by the people who live there.
When it was being carried by the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, because of wind and its heaviness,

children.text: apatad dūradeśe vai sa deśaḥ pāradaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: it fell in a distant region; that region is remembered as <s>Pārada</s>.
Therefore <s>sūta</s> that has gone into the soil is brought out by the method of distillation;
it should be understood as <s>pārada</s>, the disease-removing <s>pārada</s>.

children.text: evaṃ caturvidhaṃ jātaṃ śaṃkaraṃ śāṅkaraṃ mahaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the auspicious effulgence belonging to <s>Śaṃkara</s> came to be fourfold.

children.text: itthaṃ sūtodbhavaṃ jñātvā na rogair bādhyate naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Knowing in this way the origin of <s>sūta</s>, a man is not afflicted by diseases.
<s>Rasendra</s> and <s>rasa</s> are both accomplished <s>rasas</s>;
two others, born after a long time from earth and the like according to the region, are to be accomplished.
It is called <s>rasa</s> because it consumes old age, untimely death, poverty, and diseases,
in accordance with the meaning of the root in the sense of tasting or relishing.
Because it produces accomplishment in the body and in metals, it is therefore considered <s>sūta</s>;
because it carries one across the ocean of diseases, it is called <s>pārada</s>.
When it is being purified by distillations, one quarter of it remains,

children.text: tripādī ca kṣayaṃ yāti tena pādarasaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and three quarters perish; therefore it is remembered as <s>pādarasa</s>.
Seeing human beings, through the power of <s>sūta</s> in this state,
as equal to gods in strength and lifespan, with the deaths and diseases of mortals cut off,
<s>Indra</s> entreated <s>Rudra</s>, and in former times he joined <s>rasa</s>

children.text: yojayāmāsa taṃ pūrvaṃ vinā śuddhyāpi siddhidam ||
children.translated_text: with twelve impurities, though it had granted accomplishment even without purification.

children.text: doṣo malo viṣaṃ vahnir mado darpaśca tatphalam
children.translated_text: Defect, impurity, poison, fire, intoxication, and arrogance: their results are
stupefaction, death, constant burning, eruptions, and dizziness of the head.
The seven sheaths of <s>sūta</s> arise from earth, mountain, water, copper, iron, lead, and tin;

children.text: kañcukāḥ sapta sūtasya tābhiḥ sūto viṣopamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by them <s>sūta</s> is like poison.

children.text: kuṣṭhaṃ jāḍyaṃ ca vātārtiṃ dāhaṃ cāvṛtakaṇṭhatām
children.translated_text: The sheaths respectively cause <s>kuṣṭha</s>, dullness, pain from wind, burning, obstruction of the throat,
madness, and great colic.

children.text: etān sūtagatān doṣān pañca sapta ca kañcukāḥ
children.translated_text: The physician who gives these defects found in <s>sūta</s>, and the five plus seven sheaths,

children.text: anapākṛtya yo dadyāt sa vaidyo brahmahā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: without removing them, becomes a killer of a Brahmin.
But one should give <s>rasa</s> after removing these twelve great defects;

children.text: sa labheta mahatpuṇyam agaṇyaṃ ca mahadyaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then one obtains great merit and immeasurable great fame.

children.text: sūte 'ṣṭādaśasaṃskriyā nigaditāḥ syuḥ svedanaṃ mardanaṃ mūrcchotthāpanapātarodhaniyamāḥ proddīpanaṃ grāsajam
children.translated_text: Eighteen operations are taught for <s>sūta</s>: steaming, rubbing, stupefaction, raising, distillation, confinement, restraint, kindling, and the measure arising from feeding,

children.text: mānaṃ cāraṇagarbhabāhyajanitadrutiśca tajjāraṇā rāgaḥ sāraṇakaṃ parikramavidhir vedhastataḥ sevanam ||
children.translated_text: as well as penetration, inner and outer liquefaction, digestion of that, coloring, transference, the procedure of circumambulation, piercing, and finally use.
Now, by the procedure taught by <s>Nandin</s>, there is set forth
the proper complete purification of the defects and sheaths.
Purified <s>sūta</s> of less than five <s>palas</s> has little effect;
above that, in an amount of ten <s>palas</s>, it obtains complete purification.
By steaming, rubbing, and stupefaction, and by seven upward distillations,
the king <s>rasa</s> becomes freed from all defects.
Steaming, rubbing, and likewise stupefaction seven times:

children.text: sa hi siddhikaraṃ prāha guṇakāri ca bhāskaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāskara</s> says that this produces accomplishment and virtues.
<s>Dineśvara</s> says that it is purified by rubbing, steaming, and setting aside;
according to <s>Bhāluki</s>, purification is through upward and downward distillation.

children.text: svedanaṃ mardanaṃ mūrcchā pratyutthānaṃ ca pātanam
children.translated_text: Steaming, rubbing, stupefaction, restoration, and distillation,
confinement and restraint: purification is considered sevenfold.
This has been determined by the venerable <s>Govinda Bhagavān</s> for the king <s>sūta</s>.
Now the purification according to the method spoken by the blessed <s>Nandin</s>,
which destroys every defect of the king <s>rasa</s>, is proclaimed.
With radish, <s>agni</s>, salt, mustard, fresh ginger,

children.text: sveditastridivasaṃ hi dolayā kāñjikena malamuktaye rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the three pungents, each one sixteenth of the <s>rasa</s>, the <s>rasa</s> is steamed for three days in a swing apparatus with sour gruel, for the removal of impurity.
With burnt wool, house soot, lotus, mustard, and bricks together with jaggery...
Mercury should be ground with sixteenth parts for three days, in order to quiet that fire of it.

children.text: jīrṇe jīrṇe sadāgrāse mardanīyo rasaḥ khalu
children.translated_text: Whenever each morsel has been digested, the mercury must always be ground again,
because, through these very medicines, it becomes stainless and takes on colors.
Through grinding with the juice of <s>lakuca</s>, joined with <s>vyoṣa</s> and <s>saubhāgya</s>,
mercury, when stupefied for three days, gives up its irresistible intoxication.
With <s>saubhāgya</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>śyāmā</s>, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, together with sour gruel,

children.text: tridinaṃ saṃsthitaḥ sūto viṣaṃ saṃtyajati svakam ||
children.translated_text: mercury that has remained for three days casts off its own poison.
Raised up after being boiled with the juices of <s>sarpākṣikā</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, and <s>vyoṣa</s>,
it quickly gives up its arrogance; this is the purification of faults.
With alkalis and acids, with hot water, and kept in a windless place,
one produces a cooling of mercury's potency, and that is the destruction of its potency.
Mercury ground for a day with <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, and citron water,
then washed with sour gruel and triturated, casts off its earthy sheath.
Mercury treated with the fresh juices of <s>girikarṇī</s> and <s>jayantī</s>
casts off, in just three rounds, the mountain-born sheath that belongs to itself.
Mercury boiled for three days in a decoction of jaggery, <s>guggulu</s>, and <s>nimba</s>
casts off the water-born sheath, which carries many faults.
After it has been ground with sugar, fresh ginger, and buttermilk, and then raised up,
and washed with hot cow urine, it should cast off the copper-born sheath.
Mercury thoroughly ground with the juices of bitter gourd and <s>karkoṭī</s>
gives up the iron sheath, fickle as one gives up friendship.
Mercury made into a paste with copper and dropped through a pātana apparatus
quickly gives up the sheath produced from lead and tin.
Smear mercury with ground <s>vara</s>, <s>agni</s>, salt, <s>śigru</s>, mustard, and antimony, and place it in the upper part of the pātana apparatus.

children.text: bhāṇḍodare bhṛtajale parito vimuñcenmṛdvagninā tyajati kañculikāṃ hi vāṅgīm ||
children.translated_text: Inside the vessel, filled with water below, release it all around; with a gentle fire it gives up the tinny sheath.
Mercury dropped down in this way has the luster of a moving streak of lightning.
Freed from lead and tin, it then becomes like this.
Whenever mercury is afflicted by indigestion of a swallowed morsel,
at each such time it should be subjected to pātana by this very procedure.
Distressed by purifications beginning with steaming and ending in pātana,
mercury becomes weak in potency; therefore one should perform replenishment.
Mercury that has remained up to three days in watery rock salt

children.text: punar āpyāyanaṃ prāpya na syāt ṣaṇḍho bhavedbalī ||
children.translated_text: regains replenishment; it will not be impotent, but becomes strong.
<s>Bhāluki</s> prescribed steaming and <s>saṃnyāsa</s> after the rule,
as the settled means for eating all metals and making the mouth fit.
Having placed a vessel on charcoal, one should put mercury into it and digest it by heat,

children.text: ṣoḍaśāṃśena citrāṃ tu tadatra svedanaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: with a sixteenth part of <s>citrā</s>; this is regarded here as steaming.
Endowed with power and rich in qualities, it indeed removes all diseases.
Its ability to yield results arises quickly; there is no doubt here.
Through <s>saṃnyāsa</s> together with alkalis, acids, and salts,
in mercury indeed, according to the procedure taught in the fourth chapter,
there arise hunger, pervasiveness, sharpness, rapid action,
the capacity to remove every disease, and the state of having cast off faults.
With pepper, <s>abjā</s>, <s>āsurī</s>, <s>śigru</s>, <s>bhūkhaga</s>, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
together with fermenting agents, after three days of steaming, the mercury is kindled.
And with the group of kindling substances taught in the ninth chapter,
one should kindle mercury; that brings exceedingly good qualities.
Mercury steamed with an eighteenth part and joined with gold,
with alkalis, acids, and faultless substances, develops a mouth for eating.
With a sixteenth part of <s>tāpya-sattva</s> and with twice as much gold,

children.text: yuktaṃ yuktaṃ hi cukreṇa cūlikālavaṇena ca ||
children.translated_text: it is to be joined again and again with <s>cukra</s> and <s>cūlikā</s> salt.
With chickpea-alkali water and with citron water,
one should grind it inside a heated mortar, with great force.
For as long as twenty-one days, watch after watch, day by day,

children.text: evaṃ rākṣasavaktraḥ syātsarvāśī ca na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in this way it becomes demon-mouthed and all-eating; there is no doubt.

children.text: aṣṭādaśakriyā nṛṇāṃ na sidhyanti rasasya hi
children.translated_text: The eighteen operations of mercury are not accomplished by men
without fortune, austerity, and the grace of the Lord.

children.text: sarvairyuktā vividhavidhibhiḥ saṃskṛtībhiḥ suramyaiḥ sūto muñcatyakhilavikṛtīn śvitrarogapramāthī
children.translated_text: When prepared with all sorts of beautiful procedures and refinements, mercury gives up every defect and crushes white <s>kuṣṭha</s>.

children.text: tāvacchuddhiṃ kṛtabahuguṇāṃ nandinoktāṃ susādhyāṃ pathyāyuktāṃ puravarapatiḥ somadevo'bhidhatte ||
children.translated_text: Up to this purification, rich in many virtues, easy to accomplish, taught by <s>Nandin</s>, and joined with proper regimen, <s>Somadeva</s>, lord of the excellent city, declares it.

children.text: trikṣāraiḥ paṭupañcakāmlasahitaiḥ saṃkhalvasūtastryahaṃ bāhlīkāsuriviśvapiṇḍajaṭhare ruddhvātha saṃveśayet
children.translated_text: Mercury ground in a mortar for three days with the three alkalis and the five salts together with acids should then be enclosed in the belly of balls of <s>bāhlīka</s>, <s>āsurī</s>, and <s>viśva</s> and placed in a sealed joint.

children.text: sandhāne tridinaṃ hi mandaśikhinā dolākhyayantre paceddoṣonmuktarasaḥ sudhārasasamaḥ pathyair vinā siddhidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should cook it for three days with a gentle flame in the apparatus called <s>dolā</s>; mercury freed from faults, equal to nectar, grants success even without regimen.
But here the quantities of mustard, <s>viśva</s>, and asafoetida
are to be learned from a teacher's instruction; otherwise they do not bear fruit.
Lead and tin are two great faults, hard to conquer even by ten million purifications.
Because pātana purifies them, mercury is considered greatly purified.
With ten pātanas, the smell arising from lead and tin
comes to destruction, and the mercury is no longer of bad quality.

children.text: daśavārāt paraṃ nārvāk śatavāraṃ ca pātanāḥ
children.translated_text: After ten times, and not before, pātanas up to a hundred times
are said to produce great virtues in mercury when performed according to rule.

children.text: mahāguṇatvaṃ śikhinaḥ sakhitvaṃ svalpeṣu rogeṣu ca tulyavīryam
children.translated_text: Great virtue, friendship with fire, and equal potency in minor diseases...

children.text: rasāyanatvaṃ ca mahāprabhāvo bhavedrasendrasya ca pātanābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And through the procedures of <s>pātana</s> (distillation), the king of <s>rasa</s> becomes a <s>rasāyana</s> and of great power.
Now, therefore, the auspicious <s>jāraṇā</s> (digestion), which brings about success in <s>rasa</s>,
easy to perform, using readily obtainable substances, and practiced before, is described.
Here, the one who gives to <s>rasa</s> a <s>grāsa</s> (morsel) without leaves or laminae
has pleased <s>Gaurīśa</s> more than by the gift of the three worlds.
He who seeks the binding of <s>rasa</s> without first cutting its wings
with seeds is a wicked-minded man who, through attachment to sense objects, desires liberation.
Apart from the essence of dense mica, there is no other cutting of the wings of <s>sūta</s> (mercury).
When its wings are cut and its path is blocked, <s>rasa</s> takes on color and is bound.
Even mica-foil without moonlike sheen, when digested in mercury,
moves in sevenfold division and, though digested, may also vomit it out.
Even <s>rasa</s> into which a quarter portion of essence has been digested, when applied in the respective preparations,

children.text: tattadroge phalaṃ śīghraṃ raso dhatte'dhikaṃ yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: quickly produces the result in each corresponding disease, because it bears a greater efficacy.
Where melted essence is the seed in the operation of mercury digestion,
that too is prescribed as excellent, and as eightfold in qualities.
Mica and mercury are, respectively, the final bodily constituents of <s>Śivā</s> and <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: etayor melanān nṝṇāṃ kva mṛtyuḥ kva daridratā ||
children.translated_text: When these two are united, where can there be death for men, and where poverty?
Mercury does not indeed swallow mica essence by itself alone.
Even if swallowed with great difficulty, it will not become pervasive through all its parts.
Therefore, combined with another metal and joined with metallic essences,
it is perfected by mica and alkalis and gives only bodily accomplishment.
The making of metals into unity with mica is now explained.
With lac, jaggery, and resin of the magnet, together with <s>dhātakī</s>, bdellium, and borax,
and with equal parts ground in woman's milk, they unite even metals that are hard to combine.
A pair of metals joined with powdered <s>tāpya</s> will certainly unite,
from being blown two or three times in the furnace, surely like milk in milk.
Mica essence, combined with an equal portion of <s>tāpya</s> essence,
when made so that mica remains after blowing, becomes easy to digest.
Or else, <s>tāpya</s> twice as much, driven into the dense essence,
when digested within it quickly brings about success in <s>rasa</s>.
In this way <s>rasa</s> may digest dense essence with tin and lead.
Their essence is noble for metallurgical operations, but censured for bodily accomplishment.
These two, lead and tin, are foul and very defective, not excellent.

children.text: rogāṃśca tanutaḥ śīghraṃ sevyamānau paraṃ khalu ||
children.translated_text: When used, indeed, they quickly produce diseases in the body.
After melting that essence and filtering it through cloth, with particles remaining,
it should be thoroughly ground with the lord of <s>rasa</s> placed in a copper vessel in the proportion of one tenth.
Pure mercury, joined with its sixty-fourth part,
together with alkali, sour liquid, and salt, should be heated in a mortar for three days.
After washing it with warm fermenting liquids and placing it in a glass casket,
one should put <s>viḍa</s> above and below it, to the measure of one eighth of the mercury.
Placing birch bark at its mouth, one should wrap it with a single thread.
After wrapping the casket in cloth, according to the arrangement of the swing apparatus,
one should steam it for three days with sour gruels combined with all sour substances and cow's urine.
Then, placing it in a vessel made of iron, stone, or shell,
and washing it with warm fermenting liquids, one should draw up that liquid with a cloth.

children.text: viśoṣya lagnaṃ hastena mardayitvā kṣaṇaṃ rasam ||
children.translated_text: After drying what has adhered, one should grind the mercury by hand for a moment.
If, after it is placed in a fourfold cloth, all the <s>rasa</s> comes out through firm squeezing,

children.text: sarvo'pi yadi nirgacched garbhe grāsastathā drutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then the <s>grāsa</s> within the womb has become melted.
If some <s>grāsa</s> remains, one should steam it again together with <s>viḍa</s>.
Thus, carefully offering three <s>grāsas</s> again,
when sixty <s>grāsas</s> remain, after the melting of the womb,
in the apparatus called <s>kacchapa</s>, described in the fifth chapter,
one should roast the <s>sūta</s> joined with <s>viḍa</s> by means of cow-dung cakes with a gentle fire.
Having taken it out of the apparatus, again washing it with warm sour gruel,
one should grind it for one <s>yāma</s> according to the procedure stated for grinding.
For the purpose of making it stainless, when stainless it takes on colors.

children.text: tasmānmardyo raso yatnād grāsaṃ grāse puṭe puṭe
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>rasa</s> should be ground carefully, with each <s>grāsa</s> and in each heating.
Or, when well ground, it becomes powerful for the destruction of diseases.
The material to be processed, joined with sour gruel containing earth-alkali, salts, and groups of salts,
together with all essences, stones, and the like, and provided with excellent copper leaves, is declared to be the sour medium for the feeding of <s>rasa</s>.
With plantain, pungent substances, <s>triphala</s>, <s>lāṅgalikā</s>, half a part of turmeric, bright collyrium, foot-measured harsh <s>mañjarikā</s>,

children.text: saptāhakaṃ parivibhāvitakāñjiko'sau klinnaṃ hi lohanivahaṃ grasatīha sūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when this sour gruel has been thoroughly impregnated for seven days, the soaked mercury here swallows a mass of metals.

children.text: kṣāraiścaturbhir lavaṇaiśca ṣaḍbhir dravāmlamiśrair daśadhā vibhāvitaiḥ
children.translated_text: With four alkalis and six salts, mixed with liquid sour substances and impregnated ten times,
this <s>biḍa</s> is prescribed for penetrating the internal melting of gold and other metals and mica essence.

children.text: vīthītulye gatamalarasaḥ pañcaśāṇapramāṇaṃ bhuktvā sattvaṃ gaganajanitaṃ ṣaṣṭikākṣāravahnau
children.translated_text: When <s>rasa</s>, freed from impurity and equal to the channel, has eaten five <s>śāṇas</s> of essence born from the sky in the fire of <s>ṣaṣṭikā</s> alkali,

children.text: tattvaṃ hyetad vrajati sa javātsāradhūmāyanāni tattulyo'sau munibhirudito daṇḍadhārī ca nāmnā ||
children.translated_text: this true principle swiftly reaches the vaporings of essence; equal to that, it is called by the sages by the name <s>Daṇḍadhārī</s>.
When <s>sūta</s> is endowed with internal melting, a blade of grass thrown into it stands upright.
Because it bears an upright staff, this <s>rasa</s> is considered <s>Daṇḍadhārī</s>.

children.text: yadi bhajati hi martyastulyajīrṇābhrasūtaṃ pratidinamiha guñjāmātrayā māsamātram
children.translated_text: If, here, a mortal takes mercury with an equal amount of digested mica every day in the measure of a <s>guñjā</s> for one month...
By the lunar progression, through the method of <s>grāsa</s>, he becomes happy, wholesome, long-lived for a hundred years, and freed from the fault of old age.
He too is without wrinkles and gray hair, and free from disease.

children.text: tena tena hi yogena yojanīyo mahārasaḥ
children.translated_text: By each such procedure the <s>mahārasa</s> (great mercury) should be combined.

children.text: khasattvaḥ kurute tīvrāṃ kṣudhaṃ rogagaṇaṃ haret ||
children.translated_text: The <s>khasattva</s> (mica essence) produces intense hunger and removes the host of diseases.
In the manner of an eighth part, the second <s>grāsa</s> should be given.
The <s>cāraṇa</s> and the <s>drāvaṇa</s> should thus be arranged as before.
The <s>jāraṇa</s> too should be performed in the apparatus named <s>Kūrma</s>.
The <s>Kūrma</s> apparatus has been described in the fifth chapter.

children.text: ghanodbhūtaṃ sattvaṃ palaparimitaṃ viṃśatipuṭe rase catvāriṃśat parikalitacāraṃ ca jaritam
children.translated_text: When the essence arisen from <s>ghana</s>, measured as one <s>pala</s>, after twenty heatings, has been prepared with forty <s>cāra</s> operations and digested in mercury,

children.text: payaḥpaṅkaprāyaṃ dviguṇajaritābhre vararase yadā tadvikṣiptaṃ rasitarasarūpaṃ saninadam ||
children.translated_text: and when that substance, like milky mud, is cast into the excellent mercury in which twice as much mica has been digested, it becomes of the form of sounding mercury, with a roar.

children.text: dviguṇagaganajīrṇaḥ sevitaḥ sūtarājaḥ pratidinamiha guñjāmātrayā varṣamātram
children.translated_text: When the king of mercury, digested with twice the amount of <s>gagana</s> (mica), is used here every day in the measure of a <s>guñjā</s> for one year,
it produces an excellent rejuvenation, charm equal to <s>Kandarpa</s>, and long life reaching a full thousand years.
This <s>rasendra</s> (lord of mercury), measured as a <s>guñjā</s>, used with water of <s>arka</s>,
can cure all diseases beginning with wasting disease, even those difficult to cure.
By this ordered procedure the third <s>grāsa</s> should be given.
And in the intermediate space of the apparatus described in the fifth chapter,
the practitioner should seal it and carry out the <s>jāraṇā</s> of the substance.

children.text: pariphalaghanayuktas triṃśatā tulyavārair grasati yadi rasendro yo jalaukākṛtiḥ saḥ
children.translated_text: If that <s>rasendra</s>, joined with <s>pariphala</s> and <s>ghana</s>, takes in equal rounds thirty times and assumes the shape of a leech,

children.text: nikhilanihitamūrtiḥ niṣpatedudgato'sau punarapi nijapātre chinnapakṣaḥ sa sūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, its whole body set within, that mercury rises out again into its own vessel, with its wings cut.

children.text: jātaḥ sūtas triguṇagaganagrāsasaṃpuṣṭamūrtir bhasmībhūtaṃ yavaparimitaṃ vajrabhasmādiyuktam
children.translated_text: When the mercury has arisen, its body nourished by a threefold <s>grāsa</s> of <s>gagana</s> (mica), and when the ash, barley-sized and mixed with diamond ash and the like, is ready,

children.text: taṃ cenmartyo bhajati hi sadā jāyate divyadeho jīvet kalpatridaśaśatikān vatsarāṇāṃ prakāmam ||
children.translated_text: if a mortal continually partakes of it, he obtains a divine body and lives freely for three hundred kalpa-like spans of years.
Made inert with ash of <s>tāpya</s> in the measure of two mustard seeds,
in seven rounds it destroys all diseases for the sick person.

children.text: baddho vā bhasmatāṃ nītaḥ siddhārthapramito naraiḥ
children.translated_text: Bound, or reduced to ash, and measured by people as a mustard seed,
when taken for four months together with <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>vella</s>, and honey,
it certainly makes a human being free from wrinkles and gray hair,
endowed with the pride of a rutting elephant and having the form of <s>Kandarpa</s>.
In beauty he conquers <s>Kandarpa</s>'s pride and is free from the burning of sin.
A human being lives here for thirty-eight hundred years,
and from using it he also delights a hundred women.
By mere touch, playfully, even a fine, stout woman firm as iron
this mercury, once brought into bondage, certainly delights.
A mortal could raise the dead by merely applying it to the eyes.
Smelled, it quickly destroys all diseases; there is no doubt.
Thus the fifth <s>grāsa</s> should be administered in an eighth part.
When it is in the vessel and heated by fire, it does not depart in any way.
It is called wing-clipped, and it is freed from all defects.
This mercury, taken for three months in the measure of a <s>rājikā</s>,
with <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, and honey, brings union with the gods in the sky.
By mere smelling, the lord of mercury cuts away all diseases.
These qualities of mercury have been specified by the teachers of <s>rasa</s>.
All those qualities are true, proclaimed by <s>Bhairava</s>.
The sixth <s>grāsa</s> too should be given as before, with four <s>palas</s>.
When it has digested sixfold mica, the arising of its qualities is equal to nectar.
Measured as a mustard seed and combined with sugar candy for a month,
within a month it makes the body live for a hundred years.

children.text: baddho'yaṃ kurute caiva mukhasthaḥ khecarīṃ gatim
children.translated_text: Bound and held in the mouth, this indeed produces motion through the sky.
It wards off weapons, even divine ones, by the thousand.
Possessing the strength of ten elephants, prosperous, and honored in all worlds,
colored, made to flow correctly, and combined with <s>krāmaṇa</s>,
it becomes a piercer of ten million; unbound, it pierces spear-points.

children.text: samartho na rasasyāsya guṇān vaktuṃ mahītale
children.translated_text: No one on earth is capable of stating the qualities of this mercury,

children.text: ko'pi śrīsomadevo vā prabhāvaṃ vetti śaṅkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: or its power; only <s>Śrī-Somadeva</s>, or <s>Śaṅkara</s>, knows it.
The seventh <s>grāsa</s> should be given by means of two rounds.
Its <s>drāvaṇa</s> and <s>jāraṇa</s> should be arranged as before.
This mercury, reduced to ash and taken in the mere measure of a louse egg,
with <s>triphalā</s> and sugar candy for half a month, makes a human being
endowed with the beauty of ten million <s>Kandarpas</s> and with valor equal to <s>Śakra</s>,
honored by all the gods and possessing a lifespan of a Vedic kalpa-age,
possessed of knowledge, master of time, and endowed with knowledge of the three times,
able to curse and to bestow favor, and pleasing a hundred divine women;

children.text: kurute nātra sandeho nandino vacanaṃ yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: it makes him so, without doubt, since this is the word of <s>Nandin</s>.
This, colored and made to flow, combined with <s>krāmaṇa</s>,
surely becomes smoke-piercing; no hesitation should be made here.
After that, the eighth <s>grāsa</s> should be given in equal parts.
The <s>rasendra</s>, in which eightfold essence of mica has been digested, even with hundreds of bellows,
does not go away when blown upon, nor is it diminished at all.
This is known by the name fire-enduring, with an arising of qualities beyond counting.
And it is endowed with immeasurable splendor, wondrous potency, and great strength.
